excerpt: A six-burner built-in head with two separately controlled ovens, iQue app connectivity and a rotisserie kit included.
description:
Six stainless Dual-Tube burners rate a combined 60,000 BTU, and the cookbox is divided into two ovens that run independently, so a slow roast on one side does not dictate the heat on the other. Professional cast stainless grids sit above a stainless Flav-R-Wave system, with a 13,000 BTU side burner and a 15,000 BTU rear rotisserie burner whose kit is included.
This model is built to drop into a masonry or framed island rather than stand on a cart, leaving only the hood and control panel visible once installed. iQue controls connect over WiFi and Bluetooth, holding a set temperature and reporting it to a phone, which suits long cooks better than constant knob watching.

excerpt: Six Dual-Tube burners, twin independent ovens and phone-based iQue control in Broil King's top-tier freestanding Imperial.
description:
Broil King's flagship six-burner cart model carries a combined 60,000 BTU across stainless Dual-Tube burners and splits the cookbox into two ovens that hold separate temperatures. Professional cast stainless grids cover a stainless Flav-R-Wave system, and a 13,000 BTU side burner keeps pans and sauces off the main grates.
A 15,000 BTU rear burner drives the rotisserie, and the rotisserie kit is supplied with the grill. iQue smart control links the cookbox to a phone over WiFi or Bluetooth, tracking the set temperature and sending alerts through a long cook.

excerpt: A five-burner stainless Imperial rated at 55,000 BTU, with an infrared side burner and the rotisserie kit in the box.
description:
Five stainless Dual-Tube burners give this Imperial a combined 55,000 BTU, spread beneath professional cast stainless cooking grids. A stainless Flav-R-Wave system covers the burners, shielding them from drippings and turning what lands on it into smoke.
The side burner is infrared rather than conventional, which makes it useful for hard searing as well as pan work, and a 15,000 BTU rear burner handles rotisserie cooking with the kit already included. The body is stainless throughout, and the control knobs are illuminated for cooking after dark.

excerpt: Six-burner stainless Imperial with twin independent ovens, an infrared side burner and 60,000 BTU of main-burner output.
description:
Six Dual-Tube burners rated at a combined 60,000 BTU heat a cookbox split into two independent ovens, so one side can hold a roast while the other runs hot for searing. Professional cast stainless grids and a stainless Flav-R-Wave system sit between the burners and the food.
Searing duty falls to an infrared side burner, and a 15,000 BTU rear burner drives the rotisserie, which is supplied with the grill. The cart and hood are finished in premium stainless steel, with illuminated control knobs on the panel.

excerpt: A five-burner Imperial head unit for island installation, with a side burner, rear rotisserie burner and kit included.
description:
Five stainless Dual-Tube burners run beneath professional cast stainless grids, with a stainless Flav-R-Wave system spanning the cookbox to shield the burners and vaporize drippings. A side burner and a rear rotisserie burner are both standard, and the rotisserie kit is supplied.
This Imperial is made to be set into an island or masonry surround rather than rolled out on a cart, so the hood and control panel are what remain visible once the installation is finished. Illuminated knobs keep the settings readable in low light.

excerpt: A folding three-burner portable rated at 21,000 BTU, with snap-in legs and detachable shelves for transport.
description:
Three stainless tube burners produce a combined 21,000 BTU in a grill that folds down for transport, which puts it closer to a full patio unit than most tailgate models. A stainless Flav-R-Wave system sits over the burners and spreads heat across the cooking surface.
The legs snap in and out and the side shelves detach, so the whole grill collapses to a shape that loads into a trunk or a truck bed. A warming rack adds a second tier above the main grates for holding cooked food while the rest of the meal finishes.

excerpt: A four-burner Regal head unit for island installation, with reversible cast iron grates and Flav-R-Wave heat diffusion.
description:
Four stainless Dual-Tube burners sit under reversible cast iron grids. One face is cast for wide sear marks, the other is finned so juices collect and drip back onto the food, and a stainless Flav-R-Wave system runs between the burners and the grates.
The Regal 420 is a head unit rather than a cart grill, cut into an island or surround so only the hood and control panel show. Illuminated knobs keep the settings legible in low light, and the build sits a step above Broil King's entry ranges.

excerpt: Regal-series four-burner drop-in grill head with reversible cast iron grates and a stainless Flav-R-Wave system.
description:
Four stainless Dual-Tube burners fire under reversible cast iron cooking grids, which flip between a searing face and a self-basting face depending on what is going on the grill. The stainless Flav-R-Wave system above the burners deals with drippings before they reach the flame.
Designed as a drop-in, the 470 sits flush in an island or masonry surround with only the hood and panel exposed. It carries Regal-series construction throughout, with a stainless finish and illuminated control knobs.

excerpt: A five-burner Regal drop-in head with reversible cast iron grates and separate control across the width of the cookbox.
description:
Five stainless Dual-Tube burners give this drop-in more zone control than the four-burner Regals, which matters when part of the grate needs to stay cool for indirect cooking. Reversible cast iron grids offer a searing face and a self-basting face, and a stainless Flav-R-Wave system covers the burners.
The unit installs into a finished island or surround, leaving the hood, grates and controls at counter level. Illuminated knobs and Regal-series trim match the rest of the built-in range.

excerpt: The larger five-burner Regal drop-in, adding a warming rack above professional-grade grids for holding finished food.
description:
Five stainless Dual-Tube burners heat a cookbox that adds a warming rack above the main grates, giving somewhere to hold cooked food while the rest of the meal comes off. Professional-grade cooking grids and a stainless Flav-R-Wave system sit over the burners.
The 570 is the roomier of Broil King's five-burner Regal drop-ins, intended to be set into an island or surround. Illuminated control knobs and a stainless panel keep the installed face consistent with the rest of the built-in line.

excerpt: A WiFi-connected pellet grill in 2 mm steel, running from low-temperature smoke through to high-heat searing.
description:
Hardwood pellets feed an auger-fed firebox under cast iron cooking grids, so the same unit smokes low and slow, roasts, bakes and runs hot enough to sear. The body is built from 2 mm steel, which adds mass and helps the grill hold a steady temperature.
A digital controller manages feed rate and airflow and connects over WiFi and Bluetooth, so a cook can be set and watched from a phone rather than at the grill. The hopper holds enough pellets for long sessions without repeated top-ups.

excerpt: Four-burner Regal with iQue app control, a 10,000 BTU infrared side burner and a cast aluminium double-hood cookbox.
description:
Four Dual-Tube burners rated at a combined 50,000 BTU heat a cast aluminium cookbox with a double hood, a pairing that holds temperature once the lid is down. Solid 9 mm stainless rods make up the cooking grids, with a stainless Flav-R-Wave system beneath them.
A 10,000 BTU infrared side burner takes care of high-heat searing, while a 15,000 BTU rear burner drives the rotisserie, supplied as part of the grill. iQue smart technology connects over WiFi or Bluetooth for monitoring and adjusting a cook from a phone.

excerpt: Five-burner Regal rated at 55,000 BTU, with iQue phone control, infrared searing and a rotisserie kit included.
description:
Five Dual-Tube burners produce a combined 55,000 BTU over solid 9 mm stainless grids, with a stainless Flav-R-Wave system spanning the burners below. The cookbox is cast aluminium under a double hood, which helps the grill recover heat after the lid has been open.
Searing is handled by a 10,000 BTU infrared side burner and rotisserie work by a 15,000 BTU rear burner, with the kit included. iQue smart technology links the grill to a phone over WiFi or Bluetooth for temperature monitoring during longer cooks.

excerpt: Four-burner stainless Regal Pro with an infrared side burner, rear rotisserie burner and an enclosed cabinet base.
description:
Four stainless Dual-Tube burners run under stainless steel cooking grids, with a stainless Flav-R-Wave system covering the burners. The Pro specification adds an infrared side burner for high-heat work and a rear burner for rotisserie cooking, with the rotisserie kit supplied.
The base is a closed cabinet rather than an open frame, which keeps the tank and tools out of sight, and the side shelves are dual-level so prep space stays clear of the controls. An Accu-Temp thermometer reads hood temperature.

excerpt: A five-burner stainless Regal Pro with infrared searing, a rear rotisserie burner and kit, and a cabinet base.
description:
Five stainless Dual-Tube burners spread heat under stainless steel grids, leaving room to run part of the grate cool for indirect cooking. A stainless Flav-R-Wave system sits over the burners, and an infrared side burner covers searing that would otherwise tie up the main grates.
The rear rotisserie burner comes with its kit, so spit-roasting needs no separate purchase. The base is an enclosed cabinet with dual-level side shelves, and an Accu-Temp thermometer is fitted in the hood.

excerpt: Six-burner stainless Regal Pro rated at 60,000 BTU, with infrared searing and a 15,000 BTU rotisserie burner.
description:
Six stainless Dual-Tube burners produce a combined 60,000 BTU, giving enough grate space and zone control to run several dishes at different heats at once. A stainless Flav-R-Wave system covers the burners, and a warming rack sits above the main grates.
A 10,000 BTU infrared side burner handles searing, and a 15,000 BTU rear burner runs the rotisserie, which is supplied with its kit. The base is an enclosed cabinet with dual-level side shelves, and the control knobs are illuminated for cooking after dark.

excerpt: A larger WiFi-connected pellet grill with a stainless secondary rack and a heavy 2 mm steel body for steady smoking.
description:
Wood pellets feed by auger into the firebox, and a digital controller regulates feed and airflow to hold a set temperature from low smoke through to searing heat. The controller works over WiFi and Bluetooth, so a cook can be checked from a phone.
A stainless secondary rack sits above the main cooking grids, adding space for ribs or wings without crowding what is below. The body is built from 2 mm steel for heat retention, and the hopper is sized for long sessions without refilling.

excerpt: The three-burner Royal in a matte black finish, with 30,000 BTU of output and a cast iron side burner built in.
description:
Three stainless Dual-Tube burners produce a combined 30,000 BTU under reversible cast iron grids, and an integrated 10,000 BTU cast iron side burner takes pots and pans off the main grate. A stainless Flav-R-Wave system runs above the burners.
The grids flip between a face cast for sear marks and a finned face that holds and returns juices. The Shadow version is finished in matte black instead of the usual black and stainless mix, and a stainless warming rack sits above the main cooking surface.

excerpt: A matte black three-burner Royal that adds both a side burner and a rear rotisserie burner for slow-turned roasts.
description:
Three stainless Dual-Tube burners heat reversible cast iron grids, one face cast for sear marks and the other finned to catch and return juices. A stainless Flav-R-Wave system sits between the burners and the food, cutting down on flare-ups.
What separates the 390 from the smaller Royals is a pair of extra burners: one on the side for sauces and sides, and one at the rear for rotisserie cooking. The matte black Shadow finish runs across the hood, cart and shelves.

excerpt: The compact matte black Royal, rated at 30,000 BTU across three burners and sized for balconies and small patios.
description:
Three stainless Dual-Tube burners produce a combined 30,000 BTU in the narrowest of the Royal carts, sized for balconies and small patios where a full-width grill will not fit. Reversible cast iron grids give a searing face and a self-basting face.
A stainless Flav-R-Wave system covers the burners and turns drippings into smoke rather than flare-ups, and Sure-Lite electronic ignition lights the burners without a match. The Shadow finish is matte black across the hood, cart and shelves.

excerpt: A stainless three-burner Signet rated at 40,000 BTU, with reversible cast iron grates and drop-down side shelves.
description:
Three stainless Dual-Tube burners produce a combined 40,000 BTU, more output than the similarly sized Royal carts and quicker to reach searing heat. Reversible cast iron grids flip between a face cast for sear marks and a finned self-basting face.
A stainless Flav-R-Wave system spans the burners, and a warming rack sits above the main grates for holding food. The side shelves are stainless and drop down when the grill is parked, and Sure-Lite electronic ignition handles lighting.

excerpt: The 40,000 BTU three-burner Signet finished in matte black, with reversible cast iron grates and a warming rack.
description:
Matte black replaces the stainless trim on this version of the Signet, from the hood down through the cart and shelves. Underneath it is the same three-burner layout: stainless Dual-Tube burners producing a combined 40,000 BTU beneath reversible cast iron grids.
A stainless Flav-R-Wave system covers the burners and cuts down on flare-ups, and a warming rack adds a holding tier above the main grates. The stainless side shelves drop down flat when the grill is parked.

excerpt: A matte black Signet with three main burners, a 10,000 BTU side burner and a 15,000 BTU rotisserie burner.
description:
Three stainless Dual-Tube burners produce a combined 40,000 BTU under reversible cast iron grids, with a stainless Flav-R-Wave system covering the burners. The 390 adds a 10,000 BTU side burner for sauces and sides and a 15,000 BTU rear burner for rotisserie cooking, with the kit included.
A warming rack sits above the main grates for holding food while the rest of the meal cooks. The Shadow treatment puts a matte black finish across the hood, cart and shelves.

excerpt: A 15,000-watt starting, 12,000-watt running portable generator with electric start, a lift hook and Volt Guard protection.
description:
Rated at 15,000 starting watts and 12,000 running watts, this is a large portable set with enough capacity for heavy tools on a job site or a run of household circuits during an outage, and runtime reaches up to nine hours.
Electric start with Cold Start Technology gets the engine turning in low temperatures, and a lift hook lets a hoist move the unit where rolling it is not an option. The panel carries 120V, 240V and GFCI outlets, with Volt Guard guarding against overload damage. The generator is EPA and CARB compliant.

excerpt: An automatic standby generator producing 8.5 kW on propane or 7.5 kW on natural gas, supplied with a 50-amp ATS50 switch.
description:
The set starts on its own when utility power drops and hands the load back once it returns, running on propane at 8.5 kW or natural gas at 7.5 kW, so there are no fuel cans to refill. The outdoor-rated ATS50 transfer switch is rated for 50 amps and up to eight circuits, which covers essentials such as heating, refrigeration and lighting rather than a whole panel.
The 24-volt starting system is specified from minus 22 to 104 degrees Fahrenheit with no warming kit, and the unit runs a self-test each week. Sound output is 59.5 dBA and total harmonic distortion stays below five percent, which suits sensitive electronics. Champion backs it with a 10-year limited warranty and lifetime technical support.

excerpt: A two-burner French-built plancha on a pre-assembled trolley, cooking on a double-walled cast enamelled plate.
description:
Two circular burners in 7 mm cast iron heat a cast enamelled plate rather than open grates, so food cooks on a solid surface and nothing drops into the flame. The plate is double-walled to contain heat and edged high to hold in spatter, and its enamel is certified for food contact.
The plate meets the frame in one continuous line, leaving no seam for grease to settle in, and the surface resists scratching. The stainless body carries a marine finish in navy, the lid closes softly, and the trolley arrives assembled with two sliding shelves and a door. It is made in France from repairable, recyclable materials.

excerpt: A stainless two-burner plancha with a seamless cast enamelled cooking plate and a pre-assembled storage trolley.
description:
This is a plancha rather than a grill: two circular burners in 7 mm cast iron heat a cast enamelled plate, so fish, vegetables and thin cuts cook on a solid surface without falling through grates. Double-wall construction under the plate keeps heat in and evens out the surface temperature.
The stainless body is given a marine finish, and the plate joins the frame without a seam, so cleaning is a wipe rather than a strip-down. Certified food-contact enamel resists scratches, the lid closes softly, and the trolley comes assembled with two sliding shelves and a door.

excerpt: A three-burner stainless plancha with a wide cast enamelled plate and a trolley with two doors and sliding shelves.
description:
The 80 runs three circular burners in 7 mm cast iron under a cast enamelled plate, giving a wider solid cooking surface than the two-burner models and room to work different zones at different heats. The plate is double-walled, which holds heat in and evens out the surface temperature.
High edges contain spatter, the certified food-contact enamel resists scratches, and the plate joins the frame without a seam that traps grease. The stainless body is given a marine finish, the lid closes softly, and the assembled trolley carries two sliding shelves behind two doors.

excerpt: A three-burner plancha on a powder-coated galvanized trolley, adjustable from 150 to 360 degrees Celsius.
description:
Three circular burners in 7 mm cast iron sit under a cast enamelled plate and tune between 150 and 360 degrees Celsius, so the same surface can hold vegetables gently or take a steak at full heat. Each burner has thermocouple protection and lights from a one-hand electronic ignition, and the burners carry a 10-year warranty.
The frame is powder-coated galvanized steel on two large all-road wheels and two braked swivel castors, so it rolls over rough ground and then stays put. The trolley arrives assembled with two sliding shelves behind two doors, and the lid closes softly.

excerpt: A 30-inch rear-engine riding mower with a 10.5 HP Briggs and Stratton engine, six-speed drive and a mulching kit.
description:
The R110 is a rear-engine rider with a 30-inch reinforced stamped steel deck, narrow enough to pass through most garden gates and suited to yards up to an acre. A 10.5 HP Briggs and Stratton single-cylinder engine drives a six-speed transmission, so ground speed can be matched to how heavy the grass is.
An 18-inch turning radius and Turf Saver wheels keep the mower tight around trees and beds. LED headlights extend mowing into the evening, the seat is mid-back with a telescoping soft-touch steering wheel, and a mulching kit is included to return clippings to the lawn. Craftsman covers it with a two-year limited warranty.

excerpt: A 212cc inverter generator rated for 3500 starting watts and 3000 running watts, housed in a 56 dBA enclosure with CO shutdown.
description:
Rated at 3500 starting watts and 3000 running watts, this 212cc unit puts out pure sine wave power, which is what laptops, phones and televisions need to run without trouble. The enclosure keeps the noise level down to 56 dBA.
A 2.3-gallon tank gives roughly 11 hours of operation at a quarter load, so an overnight run at a campsite or a long tailgate does not mean a refill. CO SECURE monitoring cuts the engine if carbon monoxide collects around the unit, and the wheels and included RV adapter cover the practical side of moving it and hooking it up.

excerpt: A 420cc, 13 HP gas pressure washer delivering 4400 PSI at 4.2 GPM through an Annovi Reverberi triplex pump.
description:
The 420cc Predator OHV engine drives this machine to 4400 PSI at 4.2 GPM, the range where caked-on grime, flaking paint and stained concrete give way instead of merely getting wet. Low oil shutdown protects the engine and the brass manifold holds up under long sessions.
An Annovi Reverberi triplex pump with ceramic-coated pistons handles the water side. Five quick-connect tips cover everything from a wide rinse to a narrow cutting stream, variable pressure control dials the force back for softer surfaces, and the 50 ft steel-reinforced hose plus 12-inch flat-free tires let the unit stay put while the work moves around it.

excerpt: Commercial-duty gas washer with a 13 HP 420cc engine, 4400 PSI at 4.2 GPM, five spray tips and a 50 ft reinforced hose.
description:
Rated output here is 4400 PSI and 4.2 GPM, produced by a 13 HP 420cc Predator OHV engine with low oil shutdown. That combination suits equipment washdowns, paint stripping and large stretches of concrete rather than the occasional deck cleaning.
Water passes through an Annovi Reverberi triplex pump running ceramic-coated pistons, into a brass manifold, then out through 50 feet of steel-reinforced hose. Five quick-connect tips change the spray pattern in seconds and the variable pressure control backs the force off for siding or vehicles. Oversized 12-inch flat-free tires handle gravel and broken ground.

excerpt: A 459cc inverter generator producing 9,500 starting and 7,600 running watts, with GFCI outlets, USB ports and CO shutdown.
description:
A 459cc engine gives this inverter 9,500 watts of starting power and 7,600 running, enough to carry a house through an outage or supply an RV and an outdoor event at once. Pure sine wave output keeps laptops, phones and televisions safe on the same circuit as heavier loads.
The 6.8-gallon tank supports up to 18.5 hours at a quarter load, and Electronic Speed Control matches engine speed to demand to stretch that further while holding noise near 67 dB. CO SECURE shuts the engine down if carbon monoxide builds up. Flat-free tires and a folding handle move it; GFCI outlets and USB ports connect it.

excerpt: A portable gas barbecue on its own stand, with a 3.52 kW stainless burner and cast iron grates over a 54 by 39 cm cooking area.
description:
A single stainless steel burner rated 3.52 kW heats porcelain-enamelled cast iron grates across a 54 by 39 cm cooking area. The tall cast aluminium lid leaves headroom for a chicken or a joint, and the built-in thermometer shows what is happening under it.
The supplied stand brings the grill to standing height and gives it a stable base, while two removable side tables hold platters and tools. Push-button ignition starts the burner, the drip tray lifts out for cleaning, and the unit runs on butane or propane, taking disposable canisters directly or standard cylinders with an adapter. With stand and tables extended it measures 126 by 61 by 110 cm and weighs about 20.5 kg.

excerpt: Compact gas barbecue with a 3.52 kW stainless burner, fold-out side tables and a cast aluminium lid, on a low stand.
description:
Built around one 3.52 kW stainless steel burner under a cast aluminium lid and body, this grill gives a 54 by 39 cm cooking surface on porcelain-enamelled cast iron grates. The high lid clears a roast, and a lid thermometer takes the guesswork out of longer cooks.
Two side tables fold out when prep space is needed and tuck away on a balcony where it is not. Electronic ignition lights the burner at the press of a button, the drip tray slides out for cleaning, and the barbecue takes butane or propane, with an adapter available for larger bottles. Lid closed and tables extended, it measures 126 by 58 by 43 cm at roughly 18.5 kg.

excerpt: Two-burner gas barbecue on a wheeled cart, with cast iron grates, a tall lid and roughly 63 by 45 cm of cooking space.
description:
Two stainless steel burners mean one side can run hot for searing while the other stays low, so indirect cooking and roasting are both on the table. Porcelain-enamelled cast iron grates cover about 63 by 45 cm, and a tall lid with an integrated thermometer handles larger cuts.
The cart-style stand rolls on wheels, carries a front screen and tool hooks, and folds its side tables down when space is tight. Electronic ignition, a removable catch pan and compatibility with butane or propane round out the set. Assembled on the stand it stands 127 by 76 by 145 cm and weighs around 35 kg.

excerpt: A portable 5,000 lb car lift that reaches full rise in about 30 seconds and locks automatically at two positions.
description:
This portable lift carries 5,000 lb, which covers most cars, light trucks and SUVs, and reaches full rise in roughly 30 seconds. Automatic locks engage at mid-rise and full-rise, so the frames hold on steel rather than hydraulic pressure while work goes on underneath.
A pendant control raises and lowers the lift one-handed, with no cranking. Maximum lift height is 26.75 inches, about three inches more than earlier versions, and with the two-inch blocks in place the collapsed height is 3.5 inches. The frames come apart and stack against a wall when the bay is needed for something else.

excerpt: The 5,000 lb portable lift supplied as a complete kit, with power unit, hoses, adjustable lift blocks and extra pads.
description:
Everything needed to start lifting arrives together: the 5,000 lb frames, a hydraulic power unit in either 110V or 12V form, quick-connect hoses, adjustable lift blocks and an accessory kit that adds pads for reaching awkward pinch points.
The lift itself raises a car, SUV or light truck in under 30 seconds under push-button control, and a multi-position locking system holds the height while brakes, tires or an oil change get attention. Nothing bolts to the floor, so the frames go back on a shelf or against the wall between jobs, which suits a home garage or a mobile setup better than jack stands do.

excerpt: Extended-length portable lift rated for 5,000 lb, built for longer wheelbases and collapsing to 3.5 inches.
description:
The frames on this version run longer than the standard 5000TL, which puts the lifting points where larger sedans, SUVs and performance cars actually want them. Capacity stays at 5,000 lb and the collapsed height stays at 3.5 inches, low enough to slide under vehicles that sit close to the floor.
Push-button control brings a car to working height in under 30 seconds, and automatic locks catch at several positions on the way up. The steel frames are made to be carried and stored, so nothing needs bolting down, and adjustable lift blocks let the pads match different frame shapes.

excerpt: Extended-length 5,000 lb lift sold as a full kit with hydraulic power unit, hoses, adjustable blocks and spare pads.
description:
The extended-length frames handle longer wheelbase cars and SUVs at a 5,000 lb capacity, and this kit supplies the rest of the system with them: a hydraulic power unit in 110V or 12V, quick-connect hoses, adjustable lift blocks, the safety locking hardware and an accessory kit with additional pads.
With everything connected, a vehicle goes up in under 30 seconds from the push-button control and settles onto locks that engage at multiple points. The lift stores flat and needs no permanent installation, which matters in a shared bay, a race trailer or a garage that also has to hold a car.

excerpt: A 7,000 lb extended-length portable lift for full-size trucks and SUVs, with a 3.5-inch collapsed height.
description:
Capacity here is 7,000 lb on extra-long frames, a combination aimed at full-size trucks, larger SUVs and anything else with a long wheelbase. The extra length spreads the load across more of the frame and leaves more room to position the lift points.
Collapsed height is 3.5 inches, so the frames still slide under low-clearance vehicles, and push-button operation brings the vehicle up in under 30 seconds. Automatic locks engage at several heights and hold there. Reinforced steel construction and adjustable lift blocks suit shop use, while the whole thing still stores away without permanent installation.

excerpt: A 3,500 lb portable lift with a three-inch minimum height, sized for sports cars, compact cars and sedans.
description:
Rated at 3,500 lb, this lift is matched to compact cars, sedans and sports cars rather than trucks, and it collapses to a three-inch minimum height that clears low front ends.
The dual-frame design lifts both sides together for an even rise, and automatic locks engage at multiple positions once the vehicle is up. Push-button control takes about 30 seconds from the floor to working height. Adjustable lift blocks position the pads on a range of small-car pinch welds, and the steel frames stow against a wall in a home garage, a detailing bay or a race pit when the job is finished.

excerpt: A 48V zero turn rider with four brushless motors and 75 Ah of battery, cutting up to 2.5 acres between charges.
description:
Four brushless motors and a 75 Ah battery pack replace the engine, the oil changes and the fuel cans; a standard 120V outlet handles recharging through the rear port. On a full charge the mower covers up to 2.5 acres.
The 42-inch heavy-duty steel deck runs two blades and adjusts through twelve positions between 1.5 and 4.5 inches of cut height. Zero turn steering tracks around beds and trees without the three-point shuffle, and the control panel keeps blade engagement, slow speed mode, LED headlights and the battery gauge within reach of the seat.

excerpt: Battery zero turn mower with a 42-inch steel deck, twin blades and twelve cutting heights from 1.5 to 4.5 inches.
description:
This 48V rider runs on 75 Ah of battery and four brushless motors, so there is no fuel to fetch, no oil to drain and very little engine noise. One charge is good for as much as 2.5 acres, and the rear port takes a standard 120V outlet.
Cutting is handled by two blades under a 42-inch steel deck, with twelve deck positions covering 1.5 to 4.5 inches. Zero turn control makes tight work of island beds and fence lines, while the panel puts blade engagement, a slow speed setting, headlights and a battery readout in front of the operator.

excerpt: A 54-inch electric zero turn rider with five brushless motors, covering up to 3.5 acres on a 115 Ah charge.
description:
Five brushless motors and a 115 Ah battery give this rider about 2.5 hours of mowing, or as much as 3.5 acres, with no belts, spark plugs or filters to service along the way. The 54-inch deck is built from 10-gauge steel and carries three blades.
Twelve deck positions set the cut anywhere from 1.5 to 4.5 inches. The operator gets armrests, shaped control handles and two cup holders, and the panel adds slow speed and slow blade modes, reverse mowing, LED headlights, a battery gauge and a USB port for a phone.

excerpt: Electric zero turn mower with a 10-gauge 54-inch deck, three blades and roughly 2.5 hours of runtime per charge.
description:
Large lawns are the point here: a 54-inch deck in 10-gauge steel, three precision-cut blades and five brushless motors drawing on a 115 Ah lead-acid pack. Expect around 2.5 hours of work per charge, or up to 3.5 acres, without fuel, fumes or belt replacements.
Cut height moves between 1.5 and 4.5 inches across twelve deck settings. The seat area is set up for long sessions, with armrests, ergonomic control handles and a pair of cup holders, and the panel offers slow speed and slow blade options, reverse mowing, headlights, a battery gauge and a USB charging port.

excerpt: A lithium-powered 30-inch zero turn rider with joystick steering, cutting up to one acre on two 80V 10Ah packs.
description:
Two 80V 10Ah lithium batteries and four brushless motors drive this rider, with RYOBI rating the combined output as equivalent to a 28 horsepower gas engine. One charge covers up to an acre, and the Super Charger refills the packs in 1.5 hours.
The iDrive system steers from a single joystick, which is easier to learn than twin lap bars, and the 30-inch deck with its rubber side discharge chute passes through a standard 36-inch gate. Twelve height settings span 1.5 to 4.5 inches. An LCD screen reports runtime and battery life, the companion app does the same remotely, and the seat area includes storage, a USB port and LED headlights.

excerpt: A 54-inch lithium zero turn rider with the CROSS CUT blade system, joystick steering and up to four acres per charge.
description:
Five brushless motors run off three 80V 10Ah batteries and four 40V 12Ah batteries, output RYOBI puts on par with a 42 horsepower gas engine, and a full charge covers as much as four acres. The Hyper Charger brings the packs back in five hours.
The CROSS CUT multi-blade system is built for mulching as much as cutting, and twelve height settings run from 1.5 to 4.5 inches. Steering is by single joystick through the iDrive system, and a rubber side discharge chute keeps the mower usable close to beds and borders. Seat suspension, two USB ports, a storage compartment and LED headlights cover the long afternoons.

excerpt: A skid steer auger attachment with a 304 mm bit, 1200 mm drilling depth and a 300 cc hydraulic motor turning at 145 rpm.
description:
Post holes, tree pits and footings are the everyday work for this attachment. A 300 cc hydraulic motor turns a 304 mm auger at 145 rpm on a maximum pressure of 17 MPa, drilling to a depth of 1200 mm.
Total length is 1600 mm with 1370 mm of hose, and the unit weighs 102 kg. It couples to the loader's hydraulics for a quick changeover, which keeps setup short when a fencing run or a planting job has to be finished in a day. The build is heavy enough for compacted ground and rocky sites, not just soft topsoil.

excerpt: A hydraulic breaker attachment for mini skid steers, made for concrete, asphalt and rock demolition in tight spaces.
description:
This breaker turns a mini skid steer into a demolition tool, running off the loader's hydraulics to deliver repeated high-impact blows. Concrete slabs, asphalt and rock are the intended material, whether the job is a trench line, a footing or a driveway that has reached the end of its life.
The compact format suits work between buildings and inside fence lines where a full-size machine cannot turn. It is designed to fit TYPHON STOMP skid steer loaders specifically, and mounting follows the usual attachment routine, so a crew can switch from bucket to breaker and back during the same shift.

excerpt: A commercial 60-inch zero turn mower with a fabricated deck, Briggs & Stratton power and 10 mph ground speed.
description:
The 60-inch fabricated deck on this machine is professional-grade rather than stamped, which shows up over a season of ranch, farm or contract work. A Briggs & Stratton engine supplies the power and commercial Hydro-Gear ZT-3400 transaxles put it down, good for 10 mph forward and 5 mph in reverse.
Four-wheel suspension with deck height compensation keeps the cut even and takes the edge off rough ground over a long day. The floor pan flips up for cleaning and service, a dual-function hour meter tracks intervals, and two USB-A ports keep a phone or radio charged from the seat.

excerpt: Commercial zero turn mower pairing a 60-inch fabricated deck with Hydro-Gear ZT-3400 transaxles and four-wheel suspension.
description:
Built for acreage rather than lawns, this mower carries a 60-inch professional-grade fabricated deck behind a Briggs & Stratton engine. Hydro-Gear ZT-3400 commercial transaxles handle the drive, reaching 10 mph forward and 5 mph back, so long passes go quickly and turns at the headland stay controlled.
Independent front suspension and rear shock absorbers work with deck height compensation to hold the cut steady across uneven ground. Maintenance is straightforward: the floor pan flips up for access, and the dual-function hour meter shows when service is due. Dual USB-A ports sit within reach for charging on the move.

excerpt: A built-in three-burner grill in 304 stainless steel, with True Flame burners rated up to 20,000 BTU each.
description:
Every part of this grill is professional-grade 304 stainless steel, which is what an outdoor kitchen island needs when the appliance cannot be moved out of the weather. Three True Flame burners are rated up to 20,000 BTU each and run through adjustable valves with electronic ignition.
Wind guards and flame directors steady the heat, and a warming rack, smoker box and removable drip tray cover the rest of the cooking routine. Two interior lights and LED accents on the control panel make late evenings workable. The unit measures 76.2 cm wide by 55.88 deep by 68.58 high and weighs 50.8 kg, with a cut-out of 69.85 by 25.4 by 55.88 cm.

excerpt: Four-burner 304 stainless grill with a ceramic infrared burner and an electric rotisserie supplied with its accessories.
description:
Four True Flame burners, each rated up to 20,000 BTU, sit alongside a ceramic infrared burner for the high-temperature searing that standard burners cannot reach. An electric rotisserie ships with its accessories, so larger cuts can turn while the main grates stay free.
Construction is professional-grade 304 stainless throughout, suited to a permanent outdoor kitchen. Electronic ignition and adjustable valves handle the burners, wind guards and flame directors protect the flame, and a warming rack, smoker box and drip tray fill out the rest. Two interior lights and LED lighting on the control panel keep the controls readable after dark.

excerpt: A five-burner 304 stainless built-in grill with a ceramic infrared burner, rotisserie and 20,000 BTU True Flame burners.
description:
Five True Flame burners rated up to 20,000 BTU each give this grill the width to cook for a crowd, and the ceramic infrared burner adds the searing heat that steaks want. The electric rotisserie arrives with its accessories.
The body is professional-grade 304 stainless steel, built to be set into an island and left there. Adjustable valves, electronic ignition, wind guards and flame directors manage the flame; a warming rack, smoker box and drip tray handle everything after it. Interior lights and LED control panel lighting cover night use. It measures 106.68 by 55.88 by 68.58 cm and weighs 91.5 kg, with an 85.09 by 25.4 by 100.33 cm cut-out.

excerpt: A pair of extra-heavy-duty stands rated 35 tons, adjustable from 21 to 33 1/4 inches in 1.5-inch increments.
description:
These are support stands for trucks, buses and construction equipment rather than for cars. The pair is rated at 35 tons, and each stand is formed and welded from heavy steel with a pin-style lock that sets the height in 1.5-inch steps between 21 and 33 1/4 inches.
A 13-inch square base spreads the load on shop floors that are not perfectly flat, and the 5 1/2 by 3 1/2 inch rectangular saddle grips a frame rail without wandering. They meet the ASME PASE 2014 standard, which is the benchmark commercial shops generally work to when specifying stands for fleet service.

excerpt: A 9,000 lb two-post clearfloor lift with direct-drive hydraulics and adjustable two- and three-stage lifting arms.
description:
With 9,000 lb of capacity and a clearfloor design, this two-post lift handles cars, SUVs and light trucks while leaving the bay floor open for creepers, jacks and rolling carts. A direct-drive hydraulic system does the lifting, avoiding the chains that wear and need adjustment on other designs.
Adjustable two-stage and three-stage arms reach the lift points on everything from a low sports car to a work truck, and the low-profile arm ends slide under tight bodywork. Automatic restraints lock the arms in place, a multi-position locking system sets working heights, and a single-point release lowers the vehicle. The steel structure carries a powder-coated finish.

excerpt: A 30-inch self-propelled walk-behind mower with a 223 cc Briggs & Stratton engine and Personal Pace drive.
description:
The 30-inch cutting width is the reason to buy this mower: a large lawn takes noticeably fewer passes than it would behind a 21-inch deck. A 223 cc Briggs & Stratton OHV engine drives it, and the Dual-Force cutting system with Atomic blades chops clippings fine enough to leave on the lawn.
Personal Pace matches the drive speed to how fast the operator is walking. Spin-Stop halts the blade without killing the engine, so a gate or a garden hose can be dealt with and the mowing resumed. Height of cut adjusts at two points, the handle stows in either of two positions, and a washout port rinses the deck underside.

excerpt: Wide-deck walk-behind mower cutting a 30-inch swath, with Spin-Stop blade control and a washout port for cleaning.
description:
Fewer passes over a big yard is the whole idea behind this walk-behind: 30 inches of cutting width driven by a 223 cc Briggs & Stratton OHV engine, with Atomic blades and the Dual-Force system producing a fine mulch instead of windrows.
The Personal Pace drive speeds up or slows down with the operator's stride, and Spin-Stop stops the blade while the engine keeps running. Two-point height adjustment changes the deck in one motion, the Quick Stow handle folds into two storage positions for a tighter garage corner, and a washout port takes a garden hose for cleaning. Toro backs it with a three-year full warranty and a three-year guaranteed-to-start warranty.

excerpt: A pit-mounted low-rise lift rated at 9,000 pounds, with an open center that leaves the undercarriage clear for wheel and lube work.
description:
This low-rise lift drops into an existing pit and carries up to 9,000 pounds, enough for light trucks, SUVs, and low-stance cars. The open center means nothing sits between the technician and the underside of the vehicle, so oil changes, wheel service, and routine inspection happen without working around a frame.
A dual-pump power unit with a built-in proportioning valve keeps both sides rising together, and the reinforced upper platform handles inboard loading. It can be flush-mounted at floor level for low-clearance vehicles, and extended approach ramps are offered separately. The compact footprint suits shops converting a fast-lube pit into a full wheel-service bay.

excerpt: A baseplate two-post lift built for low-ceiling garages, with columns just over nine feet tall and a 9,000-pound rating.
description:
Garages that cannot clear an overhead beam can still run a two-post lift. The columns here stand 111 1/2 inches, about 9 feet 3 1/2 inches, which fits under ceilings as low as 9 feet 6 inches, and the hydraulic lines and equalizing cables run across the floor through the baseplate rather than over the top.
The 9,000-pound rating covers cars, SUVs, and light-duty trucks; diesel duallys and other large trucks fall outside what it is built for. Lifting comes from dual hydraulic chain-drive cylinders in a chain-over-roller arrangement, and automatic arm restraints hold the arms once the vehicle is up.

excerpt: A freestanding four-post lift with extra-long runways and a 9,000-pound rating, sized for wide and long-wheelbase vehicles.
description:
Runways on this four-post are longer, wider, and taller than the usual hobby lift, which matters when the vehicle is a long-wheelbase truck rather than a compact car. The 9,000-pound rating reaches from small cars up to diesel duallys, and the extra width gives room to spare when driving on.
It stands on its own without anchoring, and the included caster kit with polyurethane wheels lets it roll to another bay or outside. A lock ladder with a double lock system and a single-point release handles the safety side. Steel approach ramps, a steel jack tray for bottle or rolling jacks, four plastic drip trays, and two rubber wheel chocks are included, along with tracks for a rolling bridge jack.

excerpt: An overhead two-post lift rated at 9,000 pounds, with a clear floor and arms that work in symmetric or asymmetric position.
description:
The overhead beam carries the hydraulic lines and cables, which leaves the floor between the columns completely open. Creepers, jacks, and tool carts roll straight through with no plate to step over. Two height settings, 11 feet 6 inches or 11 feet 10 inches, let it fit a standard garage.
Capacity of 9,000 pounds suits cars, SUVs, and light-duty trucks in a home garage or small shop. Dual hydraulic chain-drive cylinders do the lifting, automatic restraints hold the arms, and a spring-loaded secondary lock engages on its own if a chain goes slack or breaks. A padded shut-off bar stops travel before the roof reaches the beam, and an 8-piece truck adapter set is included.

excerpt: A countertop machine that turns out soft, chewable nugget ice, up to 26 pounds a day, held in a 5.3-pound bin.
description:
Nugget ice is the soft, chewable kind that takes on the flavor of whatever it is sitting in, and this countertop unit makes it at home. The first batch arrives in about 15 minutes, and output reaches 26 pounds over a full day. The bin holds 5.3 pounds and the water tank takes 2.7 liters.
An infrared sensor watches the bin and pauses production once it fills, then restarts when ice is scooped out. Melted ice drains back into the reservoir and is used again rather than running to waste. A CLEAN button starts a five-minute flush cycle; the bin itself is washed by hand with diluted detergent, and a drain tube at the back empties the tank. The compressor is built to run quietly.

excerpt: A portable mid-rise scissor lift rated at 6,000 pounds, tall enough for undercar work and short enough for a low ceiling.
description:
Mid-rise height covers most of what tire and brake work actually needs: high enough to get under a wheel comfortably, low enough for a garage with limited headroom. The EM06 lifts 6,000 pounds, which takes in cars, SUVs, and light trucks, and the scissor mechanism keeps the footprint small.
The frame is welded steel and the platform is wide, with adjustable pads so lift points can be matched to the vehicle. An automatic mechanical lock engages at several heights during the rise. Because the whole unit is portable, mobile mechanics and shops short on floor space can move it between bays or store it against a wall.

excerpt: A low-rise portable lift with a 6,000-pound rating, sized for oil changes, brake jobs, tire rotations, and detailing.
description:
Low-rise lifts raise a vehicle to roughly bench height, which is where most quick service happens: rotations, brake work, oil changes, detailing along the rocker panels. This one handles 6,000 pounds, so cars, SUVs, and light trucks are all within range.
A hydraulic pump drives the lift and mechanical safety locks catch automatically at several heights. The reinforced steel frame is built for repeated daily use, and the compact design means it stores out of the way between jobs. Garages with height restrictions and technicians who carry equipment from site to site are the usual fit.

excerpt: A high-capacity portable power station with a pure sine wave inverter and a mix of AC, USB, and DC outputs.
description:
Built for outages and off-grid stretches, this power station runs phones and laptops as readily as small appliances and tools. The inverter produces a pure sine wave, so sensitive electronics see the same clean waveform they would from a wall outlet.
Outputs cover AC receptacles, USB ports, and DC connections, with enough of each to keep several things running at once. A digital display reports charge level, output, and remaining runtime. Recharging works through more than one input, and the case is built to be carried, so the same unit serves a basement during a storm and a campsite the following weekend.

excerpt: An overhead clear-floor two-post lift rated at 10,000 pounds, with combo arms and a three-year parts warranty.
description:
Columns on this overhead lift use a double S profile to carry the 10,000-pound rating, and the structure is robot welded under a powder-coated finish. Overall height is 143 3/16 inches and overall width 134 5/16 inches, worth checking against the bay before installation. Lock release is double point.
The arm assembly works in both symmetrical and asymmetrical positions and uses adjustable screw pads, covering a wide mix of vehicles without swapping hardware. A set of 4-inch truck adapters is included, bringing maximum lift height to 6 feet 9 inches. The structure and hydraulic system are CE certified and tested at 115 percent dynamic and 150 percent static load, and parts are covered for three years.

excerpt: A clear-floor two-post lift finished in black, rated at 9,000 pounds, with asymmetric arms that open up door clearance.
description:
Asymmetric arms set the vehicle further back between the posts, which gives the doors room to swing once it is in the air. On a lift used all day, that is the difference between a clean panel and a dented one. Capacity is 9,000 pounds, covering cars, SUVs, and light-duty trucks.
There is no floor plate between the columns, so creepers and tool carts roll freely underneath. The hydraulics are direct drive, with no chains or reduction cylinders to maintain, and the steel columns are reinforced. Two-stage and three-stage arms reach a range of lift points, and automatic restraints hold them once loaded.

excerpt: Heavy-duty steel wheel dollies sold and used in pairs, rated at 20 tons and built for trucks and commercial vehicles.
description:
These dollies are sold as a pair and must be used that way. Together they carry 20 tons, which puts them in fleet and heavy-truck territory rather than passenger car work. Each frame measures 45-5/8 by 18-1/4 by 9-1/2 inches and accepts tires up to 15-1/2 inches wide; the pair weighs 348 pounds.
Steel construction handles the load, and non-skid rubber matting on the deck keeps the tire from creeping once the weight settles. A retractable T-handle extends to 33-7/8 inches for leverage, and large wheels make positioning a loaded dolly manageable. They are certified to ASME/PASE 2014.

excerpt: A commercial-grade overhead two-post lift rated at 15,000 pounds, with extra height and width for trucks and vans.
description:
Fifteen thousand pounds of capacity puts this lift in shop territory: full-size vans, heavy-duty pickups, and larger work vehicles rather than the family sedan. The columns are taller and set wider than a standard two-post, and overall height can be set at 165 inches or 177 inches. A 150-inch configuration suits low shops but calls for extra cables.
Symmetric arms spread the load evenly and automatic restraints hold them in place. Direct-drive cylinders raise both carriages, released together from a single point. Door guards on the carriages protect panels, and a padded shut-off bar stops travel before the roof reaches the beam. A 12-piece truck adapter set and mounting hardware are included.

excerpt: A baseplate two-post lift rated at 8,000 pounds, with columns nine feet tall for garages that cannot take an overhead beam.
description:
At 108 inches, the columns stand a shade under nine feet, which is what lets this lift go into a garage with 9-foot-3 ceilings. The baseplate design carries the hydraulic lines and cables across the floor instead of over the top. Capacity is 8,000 pounds, enough for cars, SUVs, and light trucks.
Atlas calls the arm set Super-Symmetric: two stages up front, three at the rear, so a vehicle can be positioned either symmetrically or asymmetrically. Automatic restraints hold the arms, a double safety lock system backs up the carriages, and a single-point release lowers both columns together. Dual hydraulic chain-drive cylinders do the lifting, and a 12-piece truck adapter set and mounting hardware come with it.

excerpt: A full-rise scissor lift reaching 78 inches with a 9,000-pound rating, for shops without the headroom for a two-post.
description:
Ceiling height is what usually rules out a two-post lift; a scissor design sidesteps that and still reaches a working height of 78 inches. Capacity is 9,000 pounds, covering full-frame and unibody SUVs, pickups, and passenger cars. Closed, the platforms sit 4.5 inches off the floor, and the lift can be flush-mounted for a level shop floor.
Width between the platforms adjusts up to 31 inches to suit different frames. Ten air-actuated lock positions hold the lift through its travel, and the approach ramps lock horizontally to serve as extra work surfaces. Controls sit in a separate self-contained panel. Zerk fittings at each hinge point and UHMP wear blocks keep maintenance simple.

excerpt: An ALI-certified four-post lift rated at 8,000 pounds, with extended runways for stacking two cars in one bay.
description:
The extended runways are the point here: a longer vehicle sits on the lift while a second car parks underneath, doubling what a single bay holds. Capacity is 8,000 pounds, which covers passenger cars and light trucks. The lift is ALI certified and built heavier than comparable models, running close to 200 pounds more.
It is meant for collectors, restoration work, and home garages rather than a commercial bay cycling up and down all day. A caster kit with polyurethane wheels is included, so the lift rolls to another bay or outdoors; anchor bolts for a permanent installation are sold separately. Steel approach ramps, drip trays, four wheel stops, and two rubber wheel chocks come with it, and lock ladder columns with a double lock system handle safety.

excerpt: A commercial-grade overhead two-post lift rated at 12,000 pounds, with 123 inches between its symmetric columns.
description:
Columns sit 123 inches apart with 109 inches of drive-through clearance, which lets a wide truck, or one with wide mirrors, pass between them without folding anything in. Overall height can be set at 150, 165, or 177 inches; the 150-inch setting for low shops calls for extra cables.
The symmetric arms are long enough to reach the lift points on a long-wheelbase truck, and the included peg-style truck adapter set adds the height needed to clear running boards. Direct-drive cylinders raise the carriages, automatic restraints hold the arms, and a single-point release lowers both columns together. Door guards and a padded shut-off bar protect the vehicle. Coverage runs five years structural, two years hydraulic, and one year on the power unit, parts only.

excerpt: A freestanding four-post lift rated at 8,000 pounds, as useful for parking a second car as for servicing one.
description:
Four-post lifts earn their keep twice: raise a car to work under it, or park a second car beneath it and win back the floor space. This one carries 8,000 pounds, enough for most cars, SUVs, and light trucks, and it does not need to be anchored to the slab.
Lock ladder columns give a long series of runway positions, so height can be set to whatever the job needs, backed by a double-lock system and a single-point release. A flow restrictor in the hydraulic circuit keeps the descent controlled, and zerk fittings make greasing the pulleys quick. A caster kit with polyurethane wheels, steel approach ramps, plastic drip trays, and a steel jack tray are included. Two people can assemble it in roughly four hours.

excerpt: A side extension kit that widens an Atlas or Direct Lift Pro cycle lift enough to take an ATV instead of a motorcycle.
description:
A motorcycle lift is narrow by design, which makes it useless the moment an ATV rolls into the shop. This kit closes that gap: two 12-inch side extensions attach to the existing table to widen the platform, and two approach ramp extensions widen the loading path to match.
Three connector rods with pins and clips hold the extensions in place, and the changeover takes under three minutes once the parts are on hand. A two-wheeled dolly is included for moving the lift. The kit fits the Atlas Cycle Lift, the Direct Lift Pro Cycle, and the Direct Lift Pro Cycle DT.

excerpt: A portable single-post lift rated at 6,000 pounds, with a column short enough to clear a nine-foot ceiling.
description:
One column instead of two means one less obstacle around the vehicle, and this one rolls away entirely when the bay is needed for something else. It lifts 6,000 pounds, covering cars, SUVs, and light-duty trucks, and runs on a standard 110-volt supply.
The base is low-profile with built-in drive-over ramps, so a vehicle can be positioned without any lifting by hand, and the rigid frame keeps it steady under load. Two-stage telescoping swing arms reach a range of lift points and lock with arm restraints. A chain break mechanism catches the carriage if the chain fails, and a single-point release handles lowering. It works indoors or out, as long as the concrete is level.

excerpt: An open-top two-post lift rated at 10,000 pounds, with automatic arm restraints and a double-point lock release.
description:
Ten thousand pounds covers passenger cars through light trucks and SUVs, and the open-top design leaves the underside of the vehicle clear while the work goes on. A hydraulic power unit drives the lift, raised with an UP button and lowered manually, with a relief valve in the pump guarding against overload.
The hardware is sized for the load: 5/16-inch cable over 4.56-inch pulleys to cut stress on the synchronization system, and a stiffened 5/8-inch base plate under each column. Carriages ride on self-lubricating nylon sliders. Automatic arm restraints and a double-point lock release cover the safety side, rubber door guards protect panels, and anchor bolts and mounting hardware are included.

excerpt: A symmetric floor-plate two-post lift rated at 9,000 pounds, reaching a 72-inch lift height in about 50 seconds.
description:
The floor plate carries the equalization cables across the bay, which keeps the columns free of an overhead beam and holds overall height to 111.9 inches. Arms reach from 31 to 45 inches, the drop-in swivel pads sit as low as 4 inches with 1-1/2 inches of adjustment, and drive-thru clearance is 102 inches. Power is 220 volts, 20 amps, single phase.
Inside, the lift runs heavy-duty leaf chains over steel pulleys with 3/8-inch equalization cable. Columns and carriages use 5 mm steel and the arms 6 mm. Hydraulic hoses route internally behind guards, the power unit mounts on the front side to hold overall width down, and rubber door guards protect panels during loading.

excerpt: A single-column turf lift rated at 2,000 pounds, sized for golf carts, ATVs, UTVs, and riding mowers.
description:
Small utility vehicles are awkward to service on the ground and too light to justify a full car lift. This single-column unit raises up to 2,000 pounds, which covers golf carts, ATVs, UTVs, riding mowers, and similar equipment, and leaves the whole underside open for work on belts, blades, wheels, and drivetrains.
One column keeps the footprint small enough for a crowded shop or a home garage. The arms adjust to suit different frames and lifting points, and the hydraulic system raises the load at a controlled pace with safety locks holding it in position. The steel frame is finished in powder-coated black to resist wear and corrosion.

excerpt: A 54-inch zero-turn mower with a 747cc, 24-horsepower engine and a six-gallon tank for long sessions.
description:
The deck is 54 inches of 7-gauge steel with reinforced edges, hung on a heavy-gauge all-welded steel frame, and cutting height is set with a dial. Power comes from an air-cooled 747cc PRO KT724 engine rated at 24 horsepower and fitted with a commercial-grade air filter.
Dual ZT-2200 EZT integrated drive systems run without scheduled maintenance and carry the steering, which stays smooth through tight turns. The six-gallon tank cuts down on stops during a long session, and there is deep storage on board for the odds and ends a mowing day calls for. The seat is cushioned and adjusts to the operator. Coverage is a two-year limited warranty.

excerpt: A portable mid-rise scissor lift rated at 6,000 pounds, rising from 4.75 inches closed to 42.25 inches open.
description:
At 93 inches long and 45 inches wide, this lift fits a narrow bay and still handles 6,000 pounds, which covers cars, SUVs, and light-duty trucks. It travels from a closed height of 4.75 inches to 42.25 inches, putting wheels, brakes, suspension, and the lower body within reach without a full-height column lift.
The power unit rides on its own cart, so the lift follows the work from one bay to the next. It runs on 110 volts. Arm assemblies adjust to match lift points, a multi-position safety lock bar holds the platform at several heights, and solid steel support bars carry the load. Truck adapters are included.

excerpt: A flush-mounted low-rise lift rated at 9,000 pounds that sits level with the shop floor when it is down.
description:
Mounted flush, this lift drops out of the way between jobs, so the bay stays usable and nothing has to be driven over. The open center leaves the undercarriage clear, and because the platforms start at floor level there are no approach ramps to position. Capacity is 9,000 pounds, taking in light trucks, SUVs, and low-clearance cars alike.
A dual-pump power unit with a built-in proportioning valve keeps both sides even through the rise, and the reinforced upper platform with parallel arms supports inboard loading. The lock release is pneumatic, running on air cylinders off a 50 PSI charge, which retires the older spring releases that needed regular attention. An arm extension kit and a truck adapter set are offered separately.

excerpt: An asymmetric two-post lift rated at 10,000 pounds, with low-profile arms made for lowered cars.
description:
The Low-Pro arms are the reason to pick this one: they slide under a lowered car and reach lift points set at the extreme edge of the chassis, where a standard arm cannot get close enough. Capacity is 10,000 pounds, so trucks and SUVs remain within range.
The columns are single-piece and rotated 30 degrees for a better lifting angle, standing on 17-by-19-inch A36 steel base plates with an oversized 53-inch carriage on each. The top beam expands for a narrow or wide drive-thru. Dual direct-drive hydraulic cylinders do the lifting, released from a single point, with double-telescoping screw pads and a padded overhead shutoff bar to stop travel before the roof meets the beam.

excerpt: A pair of drive-on hydraulic ramps carrying 3,000 pounds together, for underbody work without jack stands.
description:
These ramps are driven onto rather than jacked under, then raised hydraulically to a comfortable working height. Together the pair carries 3,000 pounds, which suits compact cars, sedans, and light-duty trucks for oil changes, brake and exhaust work, and general inspection underneath.
A manual or foot-operated pump does the lifting, and the ramp profile is low enough for cars without much ground clearance. Locking positions at several heights hold the load where it is set. The steel frame is reinforced and powder coated against rust, and the pair is compact enough to store along a garage wall between uses.

excerpt: A 2048Wh solar generator with a 2200W pure sine wave inverter, bundled with a 350-watt solar panel.
description:
The inverter delivers 2200 watts continuously with a 4800-watt surge, drawing on 2048Wh of storage, which is enough for a refrigerator, power tools, or a bank of electronics through an outage. Sixteen outlets cover the usual mix and add a 30-amp NEMA TT-30 socket and a 12-volt, 30-amp DC port, so an RV or trailer can plug straight in.
A 350-watt solar panel is included and recharges the unit without a wall outlet, holding usable output even when the light is poor. Adding batteries raises total capacity as far as 8192Wh, so a setup bought for camping can grow into home backup later.

excerpt: A compact mini skid steer rated at 1,800 pounds, powered by a 23-horsepower gas engine and supplied with a digging bucket.
description:
Full-size loaders cannot get through a garden gate or between rows in an orchard. This machine sits at the other end of the scale, rated at 1,800 pounds and compact enough to work on farms, in parks, along roadsides, and on small construction jobs.
The 23-horsepower gas engine is an EPA-compliant Briggs & Stratton unit, which keeps parts and service familiar. Drive is hydraulic to all four wheels, with peak torque of 50 Nm at 3,000 rpm, and the controls are simple enough for a first-time operator to handle digging, drilling, grabbing, dozing, and ditch clearing. A standard skid-steer digging bucket, a tool box, and a digital manual are included.

excerpt: A wheeled mini loader with an 1,800-pound rating and a 23-horsepower gas engine, small enough for gates and tight rows.
description:
Wheels make this loader quick to reposition on paved yards and firm ground, and the 1,800-pound rating keeps it in the range of landscaping, small excavation, rock breaking, and ditch cleaning rather than heavy sitework. The footprint suits gardens, orchards, parks, and roadside jobs where a full-size machine has nowhere to turn.
Power comes from a 23-horsepower EPA-compliant Briggs & Stratton gas engine, and all four wheels are hydraulically driven, with maximum torque of 50 Nm at 3,000 rpm. Operation stays straightforward for someone new to the controls. The package covers a wide digging bucket, a tool box, and a digital manual.

excerpt: A two-burner gas plancha with an enameled double-wall cooking plate, a marine-finish stainless frame, and dial control from low heat to a hard sear.
description:
Eno builds this plancha around a flat enameled plate instead of open grates, so shrimp, sliced peppers and thin cuts stay on the cooking surface rather than falling through it. Two round cast burners heat the plate from below, and its double-wall construction holds that heat in and carries it across the whole surface. The control range runs from roughly 300F to 680F.
The frame is stainless steel with a marine finish, the burners are 7mm cast iron, and the enamel is certified for food contact. High edges contain splatter, and the plate meets the frame cleanly, with no seam to scrape grease out of. Ignition is electronic and one-handed, a thermocouple cuts the gas if a flame goes out, and a lid is available. Made in France, with a 10-year warranty on the burners.

excerpt: A navy-blue stainless cart sized for the Enosign 80 plancha, with folding shelves on both sides and a closed bay for the gas bottle.
description:
Built as a base for the Enosign 80 plancha, this cart is navy-blue stainless steel, chosen to stand up to rain and sun without staining. It measures about 50 inches wide, 22 inches deep and 30 inches tall, which puts the cooking plate at a comfortable working height.
Two side shelves fold out when there are platters and marinades to set down, then fold away when space is tight. A compartment underneath keeps the gas bottle out of sight along with its hose. Four wheels move the whole setup around a patio, and two of them lock to hold it in place once it is parked.

excerpt: Stainless steel cart made to carry the Enosign 80 plancha, with an open work surface and a concealed compartment for the gas bottle.
description:
Stainless steel construction is the reason this cart can live outdoors year round next to the Enosign 80 plancha it was designed for. It runs about 50 inches across, 22 inches deep and 30 inches tall, which sets the plancha at standing height and leaves a broad top to work on.
That surface handles prep before the cooking and plating after it. Below, a dedicated compartment hides the gas bottle so the cylinder and hose stay out of the way and the cooking area stays uncluttered. The cart moves easily, so it can be repositioned through the day or pushed back under cover once the plancha has cooled.

excerpt: Three-burner plancha on a coated galvanized steel body, with an enameled double-wall plate that spreads heat across the full cooking surface.
description:
Flat-plate cooking suits everything that would drop through a grate: scallops, sliced onions, eggs, thin steaks. Three round cast burners fire under a double-wall enameled plate, which keeps heat inside the plate and spreads it out instead of concentrating it over each flame. Temperature adjusts across roughly 300F to 680F.
The body is coated galvanized steel and the burners are 7mm cast iron. Raised edges keep splatter contained, the enamel is certified for food contact, and the plate joins the frame without gaps that trap grease. Electronic ignition lights it one-handed, a thermocouple shuts off the gas if the flame dies, and a soft-closing lid is offered as an option. The burners carry a 10-year warranty.

excerpt: Three cast burners under an enameled cooking plate, framed in marine-finish stainless steel and adjustable from a low simmer to searing heat.
description:
Cast enameled plate in place of grill bars means juices stay on the surface and flare-ups never get started. Three round burners bring the plate up quickly, and its double-wall construction traps that heat rather than letting it escape under the frame. The dial covers roughly 300F to 680F.
Stainless steel with a marine finish handles coastal damp and ordinary weather, while 7mm cast iron burners give the fire side some mass. High edges block splatter, the enamel meets food-contact standards, and the scratch-resistant surface takes a metal spatula without marking. Electronic one-hand ignition lights it, thermocouple protection cuts the gas if a burner goes out, and the burners are warranted for 10 years. Made in France.

excerpt: A direct-replacement DCR fuel pump that retires the factory CP4 on 2011 through 2025 Ford 6.7L Power Stroke trucks.
description:
The CP4 high-pressure pump fitted to Ford Super Duty diesels has a known failure mode, and when it lets go, debris travels downstream through the fuel system rather than staying in the pump. That pattern has drawn recalls and litigation across the manufacturers using it.
This kit replaces the CP4 with a DCR pump developed by S&S Diesel Motorsport together with PurePower Technologies, the aftermarket division of Stanadyne. It drops into the original location with OE fit and function, so no custom tuning or fabrication is needed, and it is emissions compliant under CARB EO D-756-7. Coverage spans model years 2011 through 2025 across the Ford F250 to F750 range fitted with the 6.7L Power Stroke diesel.

excerpt: A commercial two-post lift rated at 10,000 pounds, with an overhead cable run and a 2HP single-phase motor on 220 volts.
description:
Two posts, a 10,000 pound rating, and arms that reach both short and long wheelbases: this lift covers the mix a working shop actually sees, from sedans and SUVs to light-duty trucks and fleet vans. Two-stage and three-stage arm configurations reach the manufacturer's designated lift points instead of forcing a compromise, and the low-profile arms slide under sports cars and other low-clearance vehicles.
Hydraulics are direct drive, with no chains or reduction cylinders in the system, and the cable runs overhead so the floor between the columns stays clear. The 2HP single-phase motor takes 220V. Arm restraints engage automatically, the columns offer multiple lock positions, and the powder-coated finish is there to survive shop conditions.

excerpt: A connected French-door refrigerator with a Door-in-Door rotating bin, an adjustable temperature drawer and a fingerprint-resistant stainless finish.
description:
French doors on top, freezer below, and a second door set into the right-hand door for the things reached for constantly. That Door-in-Door panel holds a rotating bin, which turns to make room for taller items such as wine bottles without opening the main compartment and dumping its cold air.
A temperature-adjustable drawer takes food that wants its own setting, and a removable bin caddy inside it corrals cans and small packages. An LED light tower washes the back wall so nothing disappears behind the milk. Built-in Wi-Fi allows monitoring and control from a phone, including an alert when a door has been left open, and the stainless finish resists fingerprints between wipe-downs.

excerpt: An inverter generator delivering 500 to 3,300 watts of pure sine wave power, with carbon monoxide sensing and automatic shutdown.
description:
Inverter generators earn their keep at both ends of the load range, and this one runs from 500 watts up to 3,300. That covers a phone and a string of lights at the low end, and a refrigerator or a run of power tools at the high end. Output is a pure sine wave with low total harmonic distortion, so laptops and other sensitive electronics see clean power rather than a rough approximation of it.
COSense monitors carbon monoxide while the engine runs, raises an alert, and shuts the unit down if levels keep climbing. The engine is set up for fuel economy and quiet running, and the rugged frame is built to be carried to a campsite or loaded into a truck for a job.

excerpt: A gas portable generator with electric start, an 816cc EFI engine and a never-flat wheel kit for moving it across rough ground.
description:
Fuel injection is the notable part here. The 816cc Generac EFI engine meters fuel electronically rather than through a carburetor, which helps with starting and with steady running under changing loads, and the engine turns over from a key with the battery included. Runtime reaches up to nine hours at half load.
TruePower technology conditions the output for electronics, appliances and tools, while COsense watches for carbon monoxide buildup. Low-oil pressure shutdown stops the engine before damage sets in, and the outlets sit behind circuit breakers. An hour meter with maintenance resets tracks service intervals, the wheels never go flat, and Homelink compatibility lets the generator feed a house through a manual transfer switch.

excerpt: A portable jobsite and backup generator built around an 816cc EFI engine, with COsense protection and up to nine hours at half load.
description:
This is the generator wheeled out when the power drops or when the nearest outlet is a quarter mile away. Its 816cc Generac engine uses electronic fuel injection for efficient, consistent running, and it starts from a key rather than a pull cord, with the battery supplied. At 50 percent load it runs for up to nine hours between fills.
Outlets are breaker protected and conditioned by TruePower technology, so tools and sensitive electronics get stable power off the same machine. COsense monitors carbon monoxide, and a low-oil pressure shutdown protects the engine. The never-flat wheel kit handles gravel and turf, an hour meter with resets keeps maintenance on schedule, and Homelink compatibility supports whole-home backup through a manual transfer switch.

excerpt: A compact inverter generator with a 200 to 2,500 watt range, clean sine wave output and carbon monoxide sensing built in.
description:
Small enough to load into a car without help, this inverter generator handles loads from 200 watts up to 2,500. That range spans a phone charger and campsite lighting at one end, and a refrigerator or a few essential appliances during an outage at the other.
The inverter produces a pure sine wave with low total harmonic distortion, which matters for laptops, tablets and anything with a circuit board inside it. COSense tracks carbon monoxide continuously, warns as levels rise, and shuts the engine down if conditions turn hazardous. The engine is tuned for fuel economy and low noise, and the rugged frame is built to take knocks in the back of a truck.

excerpt: A three-burner Weber gas grill with cast iron GBS grates, a closed cabinet base and side tables ready for Weber Works accessories.
description:
Three stainless steel burners sit under porcelain-enameled cast iron grates from Weber's Gourmet BBQ System, which accept inserts if a griddle or pizza stone is wanted in place of the center section. The primary cooking area measures roughly 27 by 19 inches, and a warming rack holds finished food while the rest catches up.
The lid is porcelain enameled with a thermometer built in, and electronic ignition handles lighting. Two side tables carry integrated tool hooks, and the cabinet below closes with a front access door. It burns propane or butane with hose and regulator supplied, and works with iGrill 3 monitoring, sold separately. The cart is about 62 inches wide and 31 inches deep.

excerpt: A 14.4 kW Weber gas grill with three burners, a Sear Zone with boost, and a side burner for sauces and side dishes.
description:
The Sear Zone is what separates this grill from a plain three-burner. It concentrates heat in one section with a boost function, which is what a steak needs for a crust, while the remaining burners hold a steadier temperature for everything cooking alongside it. Total output is 14.4 kW over roughly 27 by 19 inches of cooking surface.
A side burner takes the pan work, whether that is a sauce, onions or a pot of corn. The right shelf carries a digital thermometer and Weber Works fittings for modular accessories; the left folds down when the footprint needs to shrink. Grates are Weber Crafted porcelain-enameled cast iron, with the frame sold separately, and the warming rack is fixed. Hose and regulator included.

excerpt: A four-burner Weber grill with a Sear Zone and about 34 by 19 inches of cooking space, rated at 17.1 kW.
description:
Four stainless burners and a Sear Zone give this cart both the room and the heat range for feeding a crowd: roughly 34 by 19 inches of grate and 17.1 kW of output. One end can sit low for chicken thighs while another section runs hot enough to mark a steak properly.
The cooking grates are Weber Crafted Gourmet BBQ System cast iron, with the insert frame sold separately. A fixed warming rack sits above them, the premium lid has a metal handle, and the left side shelf folds down. Weber Works fittings accept modular accessories and digital thermometer integration. The cart measures about 68 inches wide and 27 inches deep, and runs on propane or butane with hose and regulator supplied.

excerpt: Four burners, a Sear Zone and an integrated side burner, with 20.2 kW of output across a grate measuring about 34 by 19 inches.
description:
At 20.2 kW this is the most powerful of the four-burner Genesis carts, and the extra heat shows up where it matters, in the Sear Zone that runs one section hot enough for a proper crust. A side burner sits alongside for a pan of sauce or a pot that does not belong on the grates.
The cooking surface runs roughly 34 by 19 inches under Weber Crafted Gourmet BBQ System grates, with the frame sold separately. Stainless steel side shelves flank the firebox, the left one folding down, and Weber Works fittings allow modular accessories along the right. A fixed warming rack, a metal-handled premium lid, and a gas hose and regulator come with it. Propane or butane.

excerpt: A black three-burner Weber cart grill with a Sear Zone, a side burner and a cabinet-style base with tool hooks.
description:
