Three stainless burners, a Sear Zone for concentrated heat and a side burner mean a steak, a tray of vegetables and a pan of sauce can all run at once without crowding. Output totals 14.4 kW across about 27 by 19 inches of grate.
Grates are Weber Crafted cast iron from the Gourmet BBQ System, with the insert frame sold separately. The lid carries an ergonomic metal handle, the left stainless side table folds down, and the cabinet-style base closes for storage with tool hooks on the outside. Weber Works fittings accept the range's digital features and modular accessories. The cart runs about 61 inches wide and 27 inches deep, and takes propane or butane with hose and regulator included.

excerpt: A four-burner black Weber cart with a Sear Zone, a side burner and an integrated digital thermometer in the right-hand table.
description:
Set up for entertaining rather than weeknight cooking, this cart carries four burners plus a dedicated Sear Zone burner and a side burner, with roughly 34 by 19 inches of grate to work across. Enameled cast iron Gourmet BBQ System grates spread heat evenly and take the system's inserts, with the frame sold separately.
The right side table holds a digital display; the left folds down when the patio is tight. Both are stainless steel, tool hooks run along the shelves, and a closed cabinet below handles storage. The stainless lid has a thermometer built in, ignition is easy-start, and the gas regulator is included. The cart measures about 65 inches wide and 27 inches deep, and burns propane or butane.

excerpt: Weber's connected four-burner grill, with a Sear Zone, a side burner and live food temperature alerts sent to a phone.
description:
Weber Connect is the reason to look at this model. It reports food temperature in real time to a phone, so a roast can be tracked from indoors instead of guessed at through the lid, and a digital display on the grill shows the same reading.
Underneath the electronics is a serious four-burner cart: stainless burners, a Sear Zone for intense direct heat, a side burner for pans, and porcelain-enameled cast iron Gourmet BBQ System grates over about 34 by 19 inches of cooking area. An integrated prep and serve table gives a platter somewhere to land, and the enclosed grill locker stores accessories and tools out of the weather. Weber Works fittings accept modular add-ons. Regulator and hose included, propane or butane.

excerpt: A stainless three-burner Weber cart with a Sear Zone, a side burner and a thermometer set into the lid.
description:
Stainless steel is the main distinction here, applied to the lid, the side tables and the cart itself. Inside, three burners cover about 27 by 19 inches of cast iron Gourmet BBQ System grates, with the insert frame sold separately, and a Sear Zone section runs hot when a steak needs marking.
A side burner takes the pan work off the main grate, from simmering a sauce to boiling vegetables. The lid has a thermometer set into it, the fold-down stainless side table adds workspace when there is room for it, and tool hooks keep tongs and brushes within reach. The closed cart has access doors for storage and the cylinder. Easy-start ignition, hose and regulator included, propane or butane.

excerpt: A four-burner stainless Weber grill with a Sear Zone, a side burner and a digital thermometer set into the right side table.
description:
Stainless steel throughout, with four burners spread across roughly 34 by 19 inches of grate, a Sear Zone for high direct heat and a side burner for anything that belongs in a pan. The grates are porcelain-enameled cast iron from the Gourmet BBQ System, which hold heat well and accept the system's inserts; the frame for those is sold separately.
The right side table is fixed and carries a digital thermometer, while the left folds down. Tool hooks hang off both shelves, the control knobs sit on the front panel, and a closed lower cabinet keeps the cylinder and accessories out of sight. The lid has its own built-in thermometer. Regulator included, and it runs on propane or butane.

excerpt: An 11,000 watt tri-fuel inverter generator with remote start and an integrated carbon monoxide sensor.
description:
Eleven thousand watts puts this machine in whole-house territory rather than campsite territory, with enough headroom to carry several critical appliances at once or to run a job site with multiple tools drawing together. Inverter technology keeps total harmonic distortion low, so laptops, phones and medical devices can share the same circuits as the heavy loads.
It accepts three fuels, gasoline, propane or natural gas, which matters during a long outage when one supply runs short. Remote start saves a trip outside in bad weather. A built-in carbon monoxide sensor monitors exhaust and alerts on hazardous conditions, and the rugged frame is designed to be moved and to work in demanding surroundings.

excerpt: A foot-pump manual stacker rated to 880 pounds, with adjustable forks and a 22.5 inch frame for working tight aisles.
description:
A foot-operated hydraulic pump does the lifting on this stacker, so one worker can raise a load in controlled increments without strain. Capacity tops out at 880 pounds, which suits light to medium duty handling in warehouses, retail backrooms, manufacturing floors and storage facilities.
The forks adjust to different load widths and measure 25.5 inches long by 4.25 inches wide, fitting more than one pallet size. Polyurethane swivel casters with brakes steer the stacker and hold it in position, backed by 3 inch phenolic load wheels. The alloy steel frame weighs 187 pounds and stands 37 inches long, 22.5 inches wide and 70 inches tall, narrow enough to work down a tight aisle.

excerpt: A walk-behind auto scrubber with an 18 inch cleaning path, pad assist drive and 12 and 15 gallon tanks for long runs.
description:
An 18 inch cleaning path rated at 17,000 square feet per hour is the working math on this scrubber: one pass covers ground a mop and bucket would need several passes to reach. Pad assist uses friction between the scrub deck and the floor to pull the machine forward, so the operator steers rather than pushes it.
The 1.6 peak horsepower motor produces 113 inches of water lift for recovery, and the brush motor turns at 180 RPM. A 30 inch cast aluminum squeegee assembly pulls solution back off the floor behind the deck. Solution and recovery tanks hold 12 and 15 gallons, rotationally molded from polyethylene that resists corrosion and impact in daily commercial use.

excerpt: An electric auto scrubber that cleans an 18 inch path and lifts the solution back off the floor with a 30 inch squeegee.
description:
Built for industrial and commercial floors, this walk-behind scrubber lays down solution, scrubs and recovers in a single 18 inch pass, rated at up to 17,000 square feet in an hour. The scrub deck's own friction against the floor helps drive the machine forward, which keeps operator effort down across a long shift.
Suction comes from a 1.6 peak horsepower motor rated at 113 inches of water lift, with the brush motor turning at 180 RPM, and a cast aluminum squeegee 30 inches wide clears the trailing water. The rotationally molded polyethylene tanks hold 12 gallons of solution and 15 gallons of recovery, and resist both corrosion and knocks against racking.

excerpt: A two-burner gas barbecue rated at 8.4 kW, with porcelain-coated cast iron grids and a drip tray that pulls out from the front.
description:
A compact cart barbecue meant for everyday cooking rather than catering. Two stainless steel burners produce 8.4 kW between them, each controlled from its own knob on the front panel, and push-button ignition brings the grill to temperature within minutes. A thermometer in the lid makes it practical to hold the steadier heat that roasting and baking want.
The main cooking surface measures about 16 by 18 inches, covered by two porcelain-coated cast iron grids with porcelain-coated steel flame tamers underneath. A chromed warming rack at the back holds cooked food. Drippings collect in a tray that slides out from the front for cleaning. Fuel is propane or butane, and a two-year guarantee applies from the date of purchase.

excerpt: A five-burner barbecue with an infrared rear burner, a side burner and roughly 31 by 17 inches of cooking surface.
description:
The infrared back burner is what sets this cart apart. It climbs to high temperature within a few minutes and seals the outside of meat quickly, leaving the interior juicy, which is exactly what rotisserie cooking asks for.
The main surface runs roughly 31 by 17 inches, made up of four porcelain-coated cast iron grids plus a cast iron hot plate for eggs, onions and smaller items. A warming rack sits at the back for food that is already done. Five main burners are controlled individually from the front panel, with a side burner alongside and electronic push-button ignition next to the knobs. The cart rolls on castors, stores the gas cylinder inside the trolley, and the drip tray pulls out from the front.

excerpt: A built-in gas grill head with four stainless burners, 12.6 kW of output and a cooking surface around 24 by 17 inches.
description:
This grill head drops into masonry rather than standing on a cart, and it arrives fully assembled, so the work is fitting it to the opening. Side cabinets are sold separately for anyone building it out into an island.
Four stainless steel burners produce 12.6 kW, each with its own knob on the front panel and lit by push-button ignition. Three porcelain-coated steel flame tamers sit beneath a cooking surface of roughly 24 by 17 inches, made up of two cast iron grids and a cast iron hot plate. A warming rack handles finished food, a thermometer reads lid temperature, and a galvanized drip tray pulls out from the front. The head measures about 24 inches wide, 20 tall and 24 deep, and weighs 66 pounds.

excerpt: A four-burner barbecue cart in black and silver, with 304-grade stainless burners, a side burner and a cast iron hot plate.
description:
The burners are 304-grade stainless steel, four of them producing 12.6 kW under the lid, with a side burner outside it for pans and sauces. Each is controlled separately from the front panel, and electronic push-button ignition sits next to the knobs, so the grill reaches cooking temperature minutes after lighting.
The cooking area combines three porcelain-coated cast iron grids with a cast iron hot plate, and a warming rack at the back keeps finished food out of the way. The cart rides on castor wheels for moving around a patio, the gas cylinder stores inside the trolley out of sight, and the drip tray slides out from the front for cleaning. Assembly is straightforward, and the finish is black and silver.

excerpt: A battery riding mower with a 30 inch deck, four 60V 8.0Ah batteries included and range enough to cut up to 1.25 acres.
description:
Four 60V 8.0Ah batteries ship with this tractor, enough to cut up to 1.25 acres, though grass conditions and driving technique move that figure. The brushless cutting motor is rated equivalent to a 16 HP gas engine and holds blade tip speed constant as load changes, with bog-resistant SmartCut technology adapting automatically in thick grass. Cutting speed reaches 6 MPH.
The 30 inch stamped steel deck is a 4-in-1 design with side discharge, high airflow and an integrated wash port. Cutting height sets from 1.5 to 4.5 inches across seven positions on a single lever. Adaptive traction control keeps it straight on slopes up to 15 degrees, a rear hitch tows up to 200 pounds, and USB Type A and Type C ports and cup holders sit within reach.

excerpt: Air-cooled 22 kW standby unit that starts on its own during an outage and feeds the whole panel through a 200-amp smart switch.
description:
Generac's air-cooled Guardian sits outside the house and takes over automatically when utility power drops, feeding the panel through the included 200-amp smart transfer switch. It produces 22 kW on natural gas and 19.5 kW on liquid propane, enough to carry most household circuits rather than a selected few.
True Power Technology holds total harmonic distortion under 5 percent, which matters for electronics and appliance motors. The G-Force engine is pressure-lubricated for longer service intervals, Quiet-Test runs the self-test at reduced RPM, and Mobile Link reports operating status and maintenance alerts to a phone, tablet, or computer.

excerpt: Automatic 22 kW home standby set with a 200-amp smart switch in a NEMA 3R aluminum enclosure and a five-year limited warranty.
description:
Backup power for the whole house with no manual startup step. The unit watches the utility line, starts its own engine when that line fails, and hands the load back once power returns. The 200-amp smart transfer switch ships in a NEMA 3R aluminum enclosure rated for outdoor mounting.
Output is rated at 22 kW from an air-cooled G-Force engine, a pressure-lubricated design built for long run hours. True Power Technology keeps total harmonic distortion below 5 percent for sensitive electronics. Quiet-Test runs a five- or twelve-minute self-test at lower engine speed, Mobile Link reports operating status and service alerts, and a five-year limited warranty applies.

excerpt: Four-post storage and service lift rated at 9,000 pounds, with 5-inch runways and safety locks that catch every four inches.
description:
Model HL9K-ST is a four-post lift rated at 9,000 pounds, suited to storing a second car overhead or working under a daily driver. The runways stand only 5 inches high and carry utility lips for drip trays and accessories, so low-clearance vehicles drive on without scraping.
Spring-loaded safety locks are 3/4 inch thick and engage every 4 inches across 13 positions, while a hydraulic flow restriction system controls the rate of descent. The lift runs on 110V electric-hydraulic power and can be left free-standing or bolted down through 12-by-12-inch baseplates of 5/8-inch steel. Quick-mount poly casters handle repositioning, and the 36-inch gusseted approach ramps come off when they are not needed.

excerpt: Low-ceiling two-post lift rated at 10,000 pounds, with a floor plate in place of an overhead beam and a 220V hard-wired motor.
description:
The HL2-10K carries its crossover lines in a plate at floor level rather than an overhead beam, which keeps the top of the bay clear in garages with limited headroom. Rated at 10,000 pounds, it handles full-size pickups, commercial vehicles, and passenger cars.
Lifting comes from a chain system driven by dual hydraulic cylinders, with equalizing cables keeping both carriages in step. The columns are single-piece for rigidity, the arm restraints and arm pins are plated against rust, and a double side release allows the locks to be worked from either column. The 220V motor is hard-wired and mounted low on the left post.

excerpt: Overhead-beam two-post lift rated at 10,000 pounds that leaves the bay floor open for jacks, stands, and rolling equipment.
description:
Model HL2C-10K routes its equalizing cables through an overhead beam, leaving the floor between the columns completely open. Nothing bridges the bay, so a transmission jack or a creeper rolls straight through while the vehicle is in the air.
Capacity is 10,000 pounds, enough for full-size pickups and commercial vans as well as passenger cars. A chain system with dual hydraulic cylinders does the lifting, equalizing cables hold the carriages level, and the single-side brake release engages on the way up and lets go on the way down. Locks release by hand from one side, and the arm restraints and pins are plated to resist rust.

excerpt: Clear floor two-post lift with 12,000 pounds of capacity, sized for one-ton pickups and commercial trucks in a working bay.
description:
Rated at 12,000 pounds, the HL2C-12K is the heavier member of the Halo clear floor line, built for shops that see one-ton pickups and commercial trucks alongside ordinary cars. The overhead beam carries the equalizing cables, so the concrete between the posts stays clear.
Dual hydraulic cylinders drive a chain lifting system for steady travel, and equalizing cables hold the two carriages in sync. Locks release manually from one side through a handle, and the single-side brake release engages as the lift rises and disengages as it comes down. The columns are formed from one piece, and the arm restraints and arm pins are plated.

excerpt: Heaviest lift in the Halo clear floor range at 14,000 pounds, sized for fleet trucks, large SUVs, and high-volume service work.
description:
At 14,000 pounds of capacity, the HL2C-14K series is aimed at fleet work and busy shops where large SUVs and commercial trucks come through daily. The overhead beam keeps the floor between the columns clear, so jacks, stands, and transmission equipment move freely under a raised vehicle.
A chain lifting system with dual hydraulic cylinders provides the travel, and equalizing cables hold both sides level throughout the stroke. The locks release by hand from a single side, the brake release engages on the way up and disengages on descent, and single-piece columns give the frame its stiffness under load.

excerpt: Upgraded four-post lift with a wrap-around cross-beam, a three-part lock system, and one handle that frees all four locks.
description:
The HL9K-PRO series is the upgraded four-post platform in the Halo range, built around a wrap-around cross-beam that keeps the carriages captive on the posts so a lock cannot skip or disengage mid-travel. The posts themselves are boxed structural steel with laser-cut lock notches.
Safety comes in three parts: 3/4-inch locks that engage together at every 4-inch notch, secondary cable tension locks at all four corners, and cable keeps that hold the cables on their pulleys. A single manual handle releases all four locks at once, with no air compressor involved. The motor mounts at three different angles for a flush fit against a wall, the steel drive-up ramps stay light enough to move by hand, and post-mounted casters make relocation practical.

excerpt: Double-wide four-post lift rated at 9,000 pounds, with the extra width to work on two vehicles side by side under one frame.
description:
Wider than a standard four-post, this Pro model leaves room to work on two vehicles side by side or to move around a car without turning sideways between the posts. Rated capacity is 9,000 pounds.
Protection runs in three layers: 3/4-inch locks that engage together at each 4-inch notch, secondary cable tension locks at every corner, and a wrap-around cross-beam that prevents the locks from skipping. Cable keeps hold the cables in their pulleys, the posts are heavy structural steel with laser-cut notches, and a single manual handle releases all four locks at the same moment.

excerpt: Extended-size four-post lift rated at 9,000 pounds, with added height, width, and length for full-size trucks and large SUVs.
description:
This Pro model is stretched in all three directions, with taller posts, longer runways, and a wider opening, so full-size trucks and oversized SUVs fit without careful aiming. Rated capacity is 9,000 pounds.
The safety layout follows the rest of the Pro series: 3/4-inch locks engaging together at each 4-inch notch, secondary cable tension locks on all four corners, and a wrap-around cross-beam that stops a lock from skipping. Cable keeps hold the cables on their pulleys, the boxed steel posts carry laser-cut notches, and one manual handle drops all four locks without an air line. The motor mounts at any of three angles for a flush wall installation.

excerpt: Extended four-post lift rated at 9,000 pounds, offering 78 inches of drive-under clearance and runways just over 180 inches.
description:
The HL9K-XL is defined by three measurements: 99.6 inches of drive-through clearance, runways 180.25 inches long, and 78 inches of drive-under clearance. That last figure is what allows a full-size pickup to sit underneath a vehicle raised to full height.
Capacity is 9,000 pounds, carried on welded C channel steel posts with external locking slots. Quick-mount poly caster wheels roll the lift across a finished floor without marking it, and the 36-inch gusseted steel approach ramps lift off when they are in the way and stay stiff enough not to flex under a wheel.

excerpt: American-made 2-ton floor jack with a cast iron pump base and lift arm, reaching from 4-1/2 inches up to 20 inches.
description:
A 2-ton service jack made in the United States, built from cast iron at the pump base and the lift arm rather than stamped steel. The sealed hydraulic pump keeps grit out of the fluid, and a pressure relief valve stops the jack from being loaded past its rating.
The saddle travels from 4-1/2 inches at rest to 20 inches fully raised, with 15-1/2 inches of power raise and a saddle measuring 6-3/8 inches across. A U-joint release gives fine control over the rate of descent, the one-piece handle avoids play at the joint, and flanged side plates on a wide base keep the frame steady. Large front wheels and rear casters make it straightforward to line up under a car.

excerpt: Three-ton shop jack made in the USA, with cast iron construction, a sealed hydraulic pump, and a repairable design.
description:
Rated at 3 tons, this is the heavier of the two Hein-Werner shop jacks, made in the United States and built to be repaired rather than replaced. The pump base and the lift arm are cast iron, and the hydraulic pump is sealed against contamination.
An in-line pump assembly spreads lifting force evenly through the stroke, and a pressure relief valve guards against overloading. The U-joint release allows a slow, controlled drop, which matters when a vehicle is coming down onto stands. Flanged side plates and a wide base add rigidity, while large front wheels and rear casters let the jack be positioned precisely under a car, SUV, or light truck.

excerpt: Husqvarna 200 Series tractor pairing a 23 HP Kawasaki engine with a 48-inch ClearCut deck and a locking rear differential.
description:
A 200 Series lawn tractor running a 23 HP Kawasaki engine under a 48-inch ClearCut deck, with the deck shell covered by a lifetime warranty. An automatic locking differential senses a slipping rear wheel and locks the pair together, which helps on slopes and damp ground where one tire would otherwise spin.
The controls stay simple: an automatic choke for starting and a blade engagement lever within easy reach of the seat. The seat itself is extra-thick cushioned vinyl with a stitched face. X-Line versions add a soft-touch steering wheel, a brush guard, premium gauges, and LED headlights.

excerpt: Zero-turn with a 21.5 hp Kawasaki FR V-twin, Hydro-Gear hydrostatic drive, and a 48-inch fabricated ClearCut deck.
description:
The Special Edition runs a 21.5 hp Kawasaki FR Series twin through a Hydro-Gear hydrostatic drive, reaching 6.5 mph forward. The 48-inch ClearCut deck is fabricated from 10-gauge steel on cast iron spindles, with three blades turning at 18,500 fpm and a wash port for rinsing the underside afterward.
Cutting height adjusts through six steps between 1.5 and 4 inches using a hand-operated lift, with three anti-scalp wheels and a nose roller riding ahead of the blades. Clippings can be side-discharged, mulched, or collected. The machine weighs 581 pounds, holds 3.5 gallons of fuel, and comes with a ventilated seat and LED headlights.

excerpt: Residential zero-turn with a 23 HP Kawasaki V-twin and a welded 10-gauge, 48-inch ClearCut deck built for repeat seasons.
description:
Power comes from a 23 HP Kawasaki V-twin, paired with integrated zero-turn transmissions that need no routine servicing. The 48-inch ClearCut deck is welded from 10-gauge steel with reinforcing strips, and the zero-turn geometry lets the machine pivot around trees and bed edges instead of circling back for a second pass.
Operating controls sit together on one panel within reach of the seat, and the park brake engages and releases on its own as the steering levers swing outward and inward. Rubber bellows seal the control linkage against clippings and moisture, and the footrest is textured to stay secure underfoot when wet.

excerpt: Husqvarna zero-turn with a 10-gauge welded ClearCut deck, Kawasaki power, and a reinforced frame that limits chassis flex.
description:
A zero-turn built around a ClearCut fabricated deck: 10-gauge welded steel with reinforcing strips where the shell takes the most abuse. A Kawasaki engine supplies the power, and the integrated zero-turn transmissions are sealed and maintenance-free.
The frame and casters are reinforced to cut down on chassis flex, which keeps the deck steadier over uneven ground and holds the cut height more consistently. Controls are grouped on a single panel at the operator's side, rubber bellows keep clippings and moisture out of the control linkage, and added lighting extends useful mowing time toward dusk.

excerpt: Low-rise tilting lift rated at 7,000 pounds that stows away between jobs, made for tight garages and mobile repair work.
description:
The 7000TLX tilts a vehicle rather than raising it level, which opens the underbody for brake, tire, and suspension work without the ceiling height a full-rise lift demands. Capacity is 7,000 pounds, covering cars, light trucks, and SUVs.
The frame is steel, and the footprint is small enough to roll aside or stand upright between jobs, which suits mobile mechanics and shared garage space. Arm positions adjust to suit different vehicles and lifting points, and the safety locks engage on their own as the lift rises. The controls are simple, so setup and teardown take little time away from the actual job.

excerpt: Solar kit combining a 4,085.6Wh LiFePO4 power station, an expansion battery, and two 200W panels, with output rated to 3,000W.
description:
The kit pairs an Explorer 2000 Plus station with one PackPlus E2000 Plus expansion battery and two 200W solar panels, for 4,085.6Wh of stored energy and output rated to 3,000W. Capacity is not fixed at that figure: adding packs takes the system from 2kWh up to 24kWh.
The cells are LiFePO4, rated for a service life of up to ten years, and ChargeShield charging is credited with a 50 percent gain in battery life. The station runs at around 30dB, quiet enough to leave working near a campsite or indoors overnight, and the panels recharge it with no wall outlet in reach. Jackery covers the system with a five-year warranty.

excerpt: Top 42-inch model in the John Deere 100 Series, with a 22 hp V-twin, hydrostatic drive, and the Easy Change oil canister.
description:
The S120 sits at the top of the John Deere 100 Series with a 42-inch deck, driven by a 22 hp Briggs & Stratton V-twin through a hydrostatic transmission. Side-by-side foot pedals set speed and direction, and cruise control holds a steady pace across a long run of open lawn.
The 42-inch Edge deck uses a deep shell for cut quality and can be set up to bag or mulch. Oil changes go through the Easy Change system, a combined oil and filter canister that swaps out in about thirty seconds with no tools. The operator station is wide, the seat is a 15-inch open-back design, and the tractor carries a three-year or 120-hour bumper-to-bumper warranty.

excerpt: Residential zero-turn with a 22 HP V-twin, dual EZT transmissions, and a 42-inch Accel Deep deck rated for mowing at 7 mph.
description:
A residential ZTrak with a 42-inch Accel Deep deck and a 22 HP John Deere V-twin, set up to mow quickly without giving up cut quality. Dual EZT transmissions and 18-inch drive tires carry it to 7 mph, and the ReadyStart system starts the engine without a choke.
The frame underneath is formed and welded steel. The foot platform flips up for access to the top of the deck at cleaning time, the 18-inch high-back seat adjusts from the seated position, and the motion control levers offer several positions plus tracking adjustment on the go. The fuel tank holds 3 gallons, the machine weighs 496 pounds, and a bagger is available separately as BG20755.

excerpt: Greeneville-built ZTrak zero-turn with a 22 HP V-twin, 42-inch Accel Deep deck, and hand-lever cut height from 1 to 4 inches.
description:
Built in Greeneville, Tennessee, the Z345R runs a 22 HP V-twin John Deere engine behind a 42-inch Accel Deep deck that holds cut quality at higher ground speeds. The deck switches between mulching and bagging.
Cutting height is set by hand lever anywhere from 1 to 4 inches, and the same lever locks the deck in a raised position for transport or for clearing an obstacle. Dual EZT transmissions and 18-inch drive tires allow mowing speeds up to 7 mph, and the frame is formed and welded steel meant to hold its shape through repeated seasons.

excerpt: Standby generator in an aluminum enclosure that restores household power in about ten seconds through a 200-amp transfer switch.
description:
The 20RCAL is a permanently installed standby set in an aluminum enclosure, wired to an RXT 200-amp automatic transfer switch. When the utility feed drops, the controller starts the engine and moves the house onto generator power within about ten seconds.
Output is 20kW on liquid propane and 18kW on natural gas, and the fuel can be changed over in the field. The Command PRO engine uses hydraulic valve lifters, so there is no break-in period and no valve adjustment on the maintenance schedule. PowerBoost adds output to start a central air conditioner without disturbing other circuits, and voltage and frequency regulation keeps the waveform steady for electronics.

excerpt: Whole-house Kohler standby set rated 20kW on propane and 18kW on natural gas, with an engine from the commercial line.
description:
Rated at 20kW on liquid propane and 18kW on natural gas, this standby system is sized to cover a whole house rather than a handful of essential circuits. The set converts between the two fuels in the field, and the RXT 200-amp automatic transfer switch is part of the package.
The Command PRO engine comes from Kohler's commercial line and uses hydraulic valve lifters, which removes the break-in period and the valve adjustments that go with solid lifters. PowerBoost supplies extra starting output for heavy motor loads such as an air conditioning compressor. The enclosure is aluminum for outdoor service, and the controller brings the load across roughly ten seconds after an outage begins.

excerpt: Mid-rise two-post lift rated at 7,000 pounds, with detachable posts that store away and no overhead beam to fight a low ceiling.
description:
The M7K is a mid-rise two-post lift with posts that come apart and store against a wall, which makes a two-post bay workable in a garage that also has to hold cars, benches, and everything else. Capacity is 7,000 pounds.
There is no overhead beam, so ceiling height stops being the limiting factor, and the low base still leaves full undercarriage access. Dual direct-drive hydraulic cylinders bring a vehicle up in under thirty seconds. Three-stage arms reach a range of lifting points across different vehicles, automatic locks catch at multiple positions on the way up, and a single-point release lowers both posts together.

excerpt: Portable two-post lift rated at 7,000 pounds that sets up or stows in under fifteen minutes and runs on a 110V household outlet.
description:
This MaxJax configuration is built around the idea of a temporary work bay. Drop-in anchors and quick-connect hydraulic couplers let the posts be set up or broken down in under fifteen minutes, and built-in wheels roll them out of the way afterward. Rated capacity is 7,000 pounds.
The arms start as low as 4.75 inches, so lowered cars and standard ride heights are both within reach, and the slide blocks run without lubrication or adjustment. The lift plugs into a standard 110V household outlet rather than requiring a high-voltage circuit. The design is protected under US Patents 8,256,577 B2 and 9,150,395 B2.

excerpt: Four-post parking and service lift rated at 8,000 pounds, supplied with a jack tray, three drip trays, ramps, and a caster kit.
description:
The Pro8000 is a four-post lift rated at 8,000 pounds, set up equally for stacked parking and for service work. A single hydraulic cylinder mounted beneath the runway does the lifting, and an ultra-high molecular nylon slider keeps the carriage moving smoothly without regular greasing.
Ten locking positions release from a single point, and a relief valve in the power unit guards against overloading. The package includes a jack tray for a bottle or floor jack, three drip trays to keep fluids off a car parked below, two approach ramps, and a poly caster kit for moving the lift when it is empty. Installation calls for concrete at least 4 inches deep, rated 3,000 PSI and rebar reinforced. The finish is black powder coat.

excerpt: Extended-platform mid-rise scissor lift rated at 6,000 pounds, with an open center for wheel, brake, and suspension jobs.
description:
A mid-rise scissor lift with an extended platform and an open center, this model is set up for wheel, brake, and suspension work where a technician needs to reach in from the side. Capacity is 6,000 pounds, which covers cars, SUVs, and light-duty trucks.
A pneumatic kicker adds force through the first 6 inches of travel, the point where a scissor lift works hardest coming off a fully collapsed position. Four solid steel support bars carry the frame, dual master cylinders and dual equalizing cylinders keep both platforms rising together, and solid-steel lock bars engage automatically during the climb. Release is by push button, driven by stainless-steel pneumatic cylinders.

excerpt: A 22.9 cubic foot steel gun safe with six shelves, fourteen locking bolts, a one-hour fire rating, and an electronic lock.
description:
At 22.9 cubic feet, this Mesa safe holds long guns, ammunition, documents, and valuables together, with six shelves to divide the space instead of leaving one tall cavity. The interior measures 67 inches high, 32-1/4 inches wide, and 16-7/8 inches deep, and the door opening is 51-1/4 by 24-1/8 inches.
The body is steel in a matte textured black finish, secured by fourteen bolts, and the safe carries a one-hour fire rating that covers paper records as well as firearms. Entry is through an electronic lock with two fingerprint memory slots, which keeps day-to-day access quick.

excerpt: Floor plate two-post lift rated at 9,000 pounds, built for garages where overhead clearance rules out a crossbeam design.
description:
The NW-2-9KFP runs its lines through a plate at floor level between the columns, so nothing crosses overhead and the lift fits under a low garage ceiling. Rated at 9,000 pounds, it takes cars, SUVs, light trucks, and fleet vehicles.
Dual hydraulic cylinders drive the lift, and the symmetrical arm layout balances a load evenly between the two columns. Arm positions adjust to the vehicle, the arm restraints lock automatically once a vehicle is engaged, and the safety locks catch at multiple heights through the stroke. The structure is heavy-gauge steel throughout.

excerpt: A black-finished member of Weber's rebuilt Genesis range, running the Infinity ignition that the series was redesigned around.
description:
Weber spent years reworking the Genesis platform, and the E-435 comes out of that effort in a black exterior. Its Infinity ignition was developed specifically for this generation, so lighting the grill is a matter of turning a knob and starting to cook.
The cooking system draws on the decades Weber has spent building gas grills, going back to the first Genesis in 1985. Components are laid out with handling in mind, from the controls through to the parts that get cleaned after a long session.

excerpt: Part of the current Genesis generation from Weber, with the ignition system and cooking hardware the range was rebuilt around.
description:
The Genesis name has been on Weber grills since 1985, and the range this EPX-335 belongs to is the most thorough rework the line has had. The cooking system at its center was shaped by what long-time grill owners asked for rather than by a spec sheet.
Ignition comes from Weber's Infinity system, engineered over several years of development so the burners catch on the first attempt. The rest of the build follows the same logic, with components arranged for simple operation.

excerpt: An EPX-435 from Weber's reworked Genesis series, built on the same Infinity ignition and cooking system as the rest of the range.
description:
Weber calls this generation of Genesis the biggest change to the series in 37 years, and the EPX-435 sits squarely in it. The cooking system underneath came out of research with people who grill regularly, and the hardware reflects more than six decades of the company's work with gas.
The Infinity ignition took years to develop and is the piece that most separates this generation from earlier Genesis grills, lighting the burners consistently rather than after repeated tries.

excerpt: A Genesis EX-435 on Weber's current platform, where the ignition and the cooking system were both redesigned from scratch.
description:
Two things define the current Genesis grills: a cooking system rebuilt around feedback from people who grill often, and an ignition Weber developed over several years of engineering work. The EX-435 carries both.
That ignition, called Infinity, is designed to light the burners every time rather than most of the time. The rest of the grill rests on more than 65 years of Weber's experience with gas cooking, with components chosen for ease of use over the life of the grill.

excerpt: Four stainless steel burners and 48,000 BTU/h across an 86 by 48 cm cooking surface, with GBS cast iron grates and a 10-year warranty.
description:
This Genesis II runs four stainless steel burners at 14 kW, or 48,000 BTU/h, over a cooking surface of 86 by 48 cm, with a Tuck-Away warming rack of 80 by 13 cm above it. The grates are glazed cast iron in the Gourmet BBQ System pattern, sitting over glazed steel Flavorizer bars and a fat management system.
An open cart design keeps the gas cylinder within reach, with two stainless steel work surfaces, hooks for six utensils, two locking front wheels and two large rear wheels. The steel lid carries a thermometer at its center. Regulator, tube and clamps are included, and the grill holds a 10 year limited warranty.

excerpt: A stainless steel Genesis from Weber's current range, carrying the Infinity ignition and the cooking system this generation introduced.
description:
Stainless steel gives the S-335 its exterior, and underneath it shares the platform Weber developed for the current Genesis grills. The cooking system was shaped by input from people who use gas grills regularly, and it reflects the company's long run of work in this category.
Lighting is handled by the Infinity ignition, engineered specifically for this series so that the burners catch on the first try. The original Genesis arrived in 1985, and this generation is the most complete rework the line has seen since.

excerpt: Stainless steel SX-435 from the Genesis range that Weber rebuilt around a new cooking system and the Infinity ignition.
description:
The SX-435 wears a stainless steel finish and belongs to the generation of Genesis grills Weber calls its most significant change to the series in 37 years. That claim rests mainly on the cooking system, which was developed from feedback gathered among regular grillers.
Ignition is the Infinity system, the result of a long development program aimed at one thing: burners that light the first time, without exception. Components throughout are built for straightforward use, in keeping with the decades Weber has spent on gas grills.

excerpt: A portable Weber Q with a single 3.5 kW stainless burner, a 54 by 39 cm cooking area and a stand that holds it at working height.
description:
The Q 2200 puts one seamless stainless steel burner rated at 3.5 kW under a 54 by 39 cm cooking area, with a cast aluminium lid and body that keep the weight manageable. The lid is tall enough for small roasts and birds and carries a large built-in thermometer.
Electronic ignition handles starting, and the infinite control burner valve holds a set temperature anywhere from low to high. Split grates accept the Q 2000 series griddle, sold separately. Fold-out side tables, ergonomic side handles and front and rear cradles suit a grill that travels to a campsite or stays put on a patio.

excerpt: Two stainless steel burners rated at 6.4 kW, a 63 by 45 cm cooking surface and a wheeled cart included as standard.
description:
The Q 3000 is the largest grill in Weber's redesigned Q range, with two stainless steel burners at 6.4 kW and a 63 by 45 cm cooking surface. Lid and body are cast aluminium, and the tall lid carries a built-in thermometer.
It arrives with a permanent cart on wheels, so the grill has a fixed home without giving up the small footprint of the Q design. Two fold-down tables with three tool hooks, built-in carry handles, electronic ignition and an infinite control burner valve complete it. The split grates take the Q 3000 series griddle, sold separately.

excerpt: Three stainless steel burners over a 60 by 45 cm cooking area, with cast iron grates, flavouriser bars and an enclosed cart below.
description:
Three stainless steel burners heat a primary cooking area of 60 by 45 cm on this Spirit, with porcelain-enamelled cast iron grates holding heat over the flame and porcelain-enamelled flavouriser bars between the two. A lid thermometer reads the temperature inside, and electronic ignition starts the burners.
Two side tables give room for prep and serving, and the enclosed cart hides the gas bottle while storing accessories. Tool hooks are integrated. With the lid closed the grill measures 113 by 132 by 61 cm and weighs around 52 kg; with the lid open it stands 160 cm tall.

excerpt: A three-burner Spirit in black, with Crossover electronic ignition, Flavorizer bars and a GBS grate that opens up for accessories.
description:
Three tapered burners run front to back on this Spirit, a shape Weber uses to keep gas flow steady so heat reaches the whole grate rather than pooling at one end. Crossover electronic ignition lights them. Flavorizer bars sit above, catching the drippings that turn to smoke on contact and steering the rest into the grease management system, where a catch pan slides out from under the cookbox for emptying.
The cooking grate belongs to the Gourmet BBQ System, so the circular insert lifts out and a griddle, poultry roaster or pizza stone takes its place. A Tuck-Away warming rack folds out of the way, and side tables plus tool hooks keep tongs and trays close.

excerpt: Three main burners plus a dedicated side burner for garnishes, with a GBS grate, Flavorizer bars and a Tuck-Away warming rack.
description:
What separates the E-325 from the smaller Spirit models is the side burner, which handles sauces and garnishes while the three main burners work the grate. Those burners use a tapered profile that keeps gas flow steady from front to back, and Crossover electronic ignition starts them.
Flavorizer bars catch drippings and send whatever does not vaporise into a catch pan below the cookbox. The Gourmet BBQ System grate takes inserts in place of its circular centre section, and the Tuck-Away warming rack holds finished food above the main meal. Side tables and tool hooks are part of the cart.

excerpt: Four stainless steel burners and a sear zone over an 86 by 48 cm grate, with GBS cast iron grates and a closed double-door cart.
description:
Four stainless steel burners cover an 86 by 48 cm cooking area on this Spirit, with a dedicated sear zone for direct high heat when something needs a hard crust. Grates are porcelain-enamelled cast iron in the Gourmet BBQ System pattern, and the porcelain-enamelled lid carries a built-in thermometer.
Electronic crossover ignition starts the burners. Two folding side tables with integrated tool hooks give working room, and the closed cart has double doors for storage. The grill is 155 cm wide, 81 cm deep and 160 cm tall with the lid open, weighing around 56 kg. A regulator is included, and iGrill 3 fits it, sold separately.

excerpt: Three burners, a sear zone and a side burner in a Spirit sized around a 60 by 45 cm cooking area and roughly 48 kg.
description:
The EP-325 pairs three stainless steel burners with a sear zone for high heat and a side burner for sauces or sides, all over a primary cooking area of 60 by 45 cm. Porcelain-enamelled cast iron Gourmet BBQ System grates spread the heat and take the usual GBS accessories.
A thermometer sits in the porcelain-enamelled lid, and electronic ignition starts the burners. Foldable side tables carry integrated tool hooks, and the closed cabinet behind double doors holds the gas bottle and accessories. Dimensions are 127 cm wide by 81 cm deep, 160 cm tall with the lid open, at roughly 48 kg.

excerpt: Four burners, a sear zone and a side burner across an 86 by 48 cm grate, in a black Spirit built around regular entertaining.
description:
Four stainless steel burners, a dedicated sear zone and a side burner give the EP-435 enough separate heat sources to cook a main course and its sides at once, across a primary cooking area of 86 by 48 cm. The Gourmet BBQ System grates are porcelain-enamelled cast iron and accept the range of GBS accessories.
The porcelain-enamelled lid has a built-in thermometer, and electronic ignition handles starting. Two side tables, one of them foldable, carry tool hooks, and a closed cabinet with double doors stores accessories. It measures 165 cm wide by 81 cm deep and stands 160 cm tall with the lid open, at about 60 kg.

excerpt: A connected three-burner Spirit that sends food temperature readings and countdowns to a phone while the cook is under way.
description:
Weber Connect is built into this Spirit, reporting food temperature in real time and counting down to the point where something needs turning or taking off. Three stainless steel burners sit under porcelain-enamelled cast iron Gourmet BBQ System grates, with a thermometer in the porcelain-enamelled lid for a direct reading.
Electronic ignition starts the burners. A warming rack holds finished food, side tables carry tool hooks, and the closed cabinet includes a storage shelf. The grill is 126 cm wide and 81 cm deep, 160 cm tall with the lid open, at roughly 52 kg, and a regulator is included.

excerpt: A black smart Spirit that puts live cooking temperatures on both the phone and the barbecue, with an alert at the target point.
description:
The smart hardware on this Spirit reports food temperature and time remaining on a phone and on the barbecue itself, with an alert once the food reaches the point it was set for. Step-by-step assistance covers the stages of a cook, which helps when attention is split between the grill and everything else going on outside.
Crossover electronic ignition lights the burners, which use a tapered shape that keeps gas flow consistent from front to back so food cooks evenly across the grate. Flavorizer bars sit below, turning drippings into smoke and routing the rest away from the burners.

excerpt: Three burners with a sear zone, a side burner and Weber Connect notifications, in a black cabinet-style Spirit at about 56.5 kg.
description:
Three stainless steel burners, a sear zone for intense heat and a side burner for simmering give this Spirit room to run several things at once, over a primary cooking area of 60 by 45 cm. Weber Connect is integrated, sending cooking notifications to a phone as temperatures change.
Grates are porcelain-enamelled cast iron in the Gourmet BBQ System pattern, and the porcelain-enamelled lid holds a thermometer. Electronic ignition, side tables with tool hooks, a warming rack and a closed cabinet with an internal shelf complete the cart. It is 132 cm wide and 81 cm deep, 160 cm tall with the lid open.

excerpt: A black Spirit II grill built around Weber's GS4 system, with a Gourmet BBQ System grate and ignition meant to catch every time.
description:
Weber built the Spirit II series around GS4, a grilling system the company developed from decades of work with gas and from what people who grill regularly said they wanted. It covers ignition, burner behaviour, the way drippings turn into smoke, and cleanup.
In practice that means burners meant to light every time, heat that stays even across the grate wherever food is placed, and a grease path that keeps cleanup short. The E-210 carries a Gourmet BBQ System grate and a black exterior.

excerpt: A black Spirit II with a Gourmet BBQ System grate, using the GS4 grilling system Weber introduced with this generation.
description:
The Spirit II generation marked a full rework of Weber's long-running Spirit line, and GS4 is the reason. The system ties together ignition, burner design, the smoke that drippings create as they vaporise, and the cleanup that follows a cook.
Each part was designed for easy use rather than for a longer feature list, which shows up in burners that light reliably and in heat that stays consistent regardless of where food sits on the cooking grate. This E-220 pairs that with a Gourmet BBQ System grate and a black finish.

excerpt: Black-finished Spirit II with a GBS grate, running the GS4 system that separates this generation from the Spirit grills before it.
description:
GS4 is what sets the Spirit II apart from earlier Spirit models. Weber rebuilt ignition, burners, the smoke path and the cleanup process as one system, drawing on 30 years of grilling experience and on feedback from people who cook outdoors often.
The result is meant to be uncomplicated: burners that catch when the knob turns, even heat across the full cooking grate, and cleanup that does not stretch the evening out. The E-310 adds a Gourmet BBQ System grate and a black exterior.

excerpt: GS4 underneath and a Gourmet BBQ System grate up top, in a Weber grill whose whole generation was reworked around easy operation.
description:
Black outside, with a Gourmet BBQ System grate above the burners, the E-320 follows the format Weber set for the Spirit II range.
Underneath sits GS4, the grilling system developed for this generation. It covers ignition, burner design, the smoke that drippings create as they vaporise and the cleanup afterwards, with each part shaped around simple operation. Weber drew on 30 years of grilling experience and on direct input from the people who use its grills when putting the system together.

excerpt: A premium Spirit in black with a stainless GBS grate in two 30 by 44 cm sections around a 30 cm central opening.
description:
The grate is the headline here: stainless steel, in two sections of 30 by 44 cm with a 30 cm circular aperture in the middle. With the insert removed, a griddle, poultry roaster or pizza stone drops into its place, which is the point of the Gourmet BBQ System.
The rest follows Weber's Spirit Premium format. Tapered burners keep gas flow steady from front to back for even heat, electronic ignition starts them, and a Sear Station creates a concentrated hot zone for marking meat. Flavorizer bars vaporise drippings into smoke and funnel the rest into a catch pan under the cook box.

excerpt: Stainless steel Spirit Premium with front-mounted controls, two work tables and a cookbox with room for a 10 kg turkey.
description:
Stainless steel runs through this Spirit Premium, from the shroud, which will not fade, peel or rust, to the cooking grates, which hold heat well and wipe down quickly. The control panel has moved to the front, and two work tables flank a cookbox with space for a 10 kg turkey, or for meat and vegetables at the same time.
The adaptable Gourmet BBQ System grate arrives as two stainless sections of 30 by 44 cm with a 30 cm central aperture for accessories. Electronic ignition lights tapered burners that keep gas flow even front to back, and Flavorizer bars handle drippings above the grease management system.

excerpt: The SPX-335 in stainless steel, with a two-section GBS grate, tapered burners and a cook box sized for a large roast.
description:
Weber reworked this model in stainless steel throughout, and the choice shows in how it wears: the shroud does not fade, peel or rust, and the stainless grates retain heat and clean up quickly. Controls sit on the front panel, with two spacious work tables either side.
The cook box handles a 10 kg turkey, or a mix of roasting meat and vegetables. Its Gourmet BBQ System grate is stainless as well, two sections of 30 by 44 cm with a 30 cm opening at the centre for accessories. Electronic ignition, tapered high performance burners and Flavorizer bars above the grease management system complete the setup.

excerpt: The SP-435 keeps its stainless steel finish throughout, from the shroud down to the folding side tables and the enclosed cabinet.
description:
Four stainless steel burners, a high-heat sear zone and a stainless steel side burner give the SP-435 several separate heat sources, across a primary cooking surface of 86 by 48 cm. The Gourmet BBQ System grates are porcelain-enamelled cast iron and take GBS accessories.
Stainless steel carries through the build, including the side tables, one of which folds. Tool hooks are integrated, and an enclosed cabinet with double doors keeps accessories out of sight. Electronic ignition, a thermometer in the porcelain-enamelled lid, 165 cm of width, 81 cm of depth and around 60 kg round it out.

excerpt: Stainless steel smart Spirit with three burners, a sear zone, a side burner and Weber Connect guidance sent through to a phone.
description:
Weber Connect is built into this stainless steel Spirit, sending temperature updates and step-by-step prompts to a phone during a cook. Three stainless steel burners heat a 60 by 45 cm cooking area, with a sear zone for high heat and a side burner for a pan of sauce.
Porcelain-enamelled cast iron Gourmet BBQ System grates take the full run of GBS accessories. The stainless lid carries a thermometer, electronic ignition starts the burners, and stainless side tables with tool hooks flank a closed cabinet with a storage shelf. It measures 132 cm wide by 81 cm deep, 160 cm tall with the lid open, near 56.5 kg.

excerpt: Output is split three ways here: 9.4 kW of main burner, a 2.2 kW sear zone and a 3.5 kW side burner on a black enclosed cart.
description:
Three stainless steel burners rated at 9.4 kW cover a primary cooking area of 60 by 45 cm on this Spirit, with a 2.2 kW sear zone for caramelisation and a 3.5 kW side burner for sauces. Gourmet BBQ System cast iron grates sit above porcelain-enamelled flavouriser bars, and the grates accept pizza stones, griddles and the rest of the GBS accessories.
Crossover electronic ignition starts it and the lid thermometer shows what is happening inside. Two stainless steel side shelves carry tool hooks, the enclosed cart provides storage, and lockable castor wheels let the grill move and then stay put. Closed, it stands 116 cm tall and 126 cm wide.

excerpt: Four burners with a sear zone and a side burner, spread over an 86 by 48 cm cooking area on a double-door storage cart.
description:
The EP-425 runs four stainless steel burners over a primary cooking area of 86 by 48 cm, with a sear zone for direct high heat and a side burner for sauces or vegetables cooked in a pan. Porcelain-enamelled cast iron Gourmet BBQ System grates hold that heat and take GBS accessories.
A thermometer is set into the porcelain-enamelled lid, and electronic ignition starts the burners. Two side tables with utensil hooks, one of them folding, sit either side of a closed cart with double-door storage. The grill is 155 cm wide and 81 cm deep, 160 cm tall with the lid open, at about 56 kg.

excerpt: A folding portable Weber with one stainless burner, cast iron grates and a cart that collapses to 32 cm high for transport.
description:
The Traveler Compact folds with one hand, dropping from 98 cm tall to 32 cm so the cart fits in a car boot or stands against a wall in storage. Open, it is 106 cm wide and 58 cm deep and weighs around 17 kg.
A single stainless steel burner heats porcelain-enamelled cast iron grates across roughly 49 by 33 cm of cooking space, with a thermometer in the lid and a removable drip tray underneath. It runs on a gas cartridge, and an adapter for larger cylinders is sold separately. A large side table gives room for prep and serving.

excerpt: A 60-inch zero-turn built around a Kohler 7000 Series V-Twin and a 10-gauge steel deck, sized for properties measured in acres.
description:
The Titan Max runs a Kohler 7000 Series V-Twin rated at 26HP, with a canister-style air cleaner ahead of it to keep dust and clippings out of the intake on long jobs. Dual hydrostatic transmissions handle the drive, so speed and direction changes stay smooth through turns and around obstacles.
The IronForged cutting deck spans 60 inches and is formed from 10-gauge steel with a bull nose reinforced leading edge. Underneath it sits a tubular steel frame, and the operator station uses a high-back seat with a step-through opening for getting on and off.

excerpt: Zero-turn riding mower with dual hydrostatic drive and a 60-inch IronForged deck, meant for large lawns and small acreage.
description:
Cutting width here is 60 inches, and the deck behind it is IronForged: 10-gauge steel with a bull nose reinforcement along the leading edge, built to survive contact with roots, curbs and fence lines. Power comes from a 26HP Kohler 7000 Series V-Twin fitted with a canister air cleaner.
Dual hydrostatic transmissions give the machine true zero-turn behavior, and the chassis is tubular steel. The seating position is high-back, and a step-through design keeps the path on and off the mower clear.

excerpt: Model TFB61RLGI, a wood pellet grill with app-based temperature control, dual-wall insulation and a 10 kg pellet hopper.
description:
Traeger builds this model, TFB61RLGI, around a touchscreen controller and WiFIRE connectivity, so temperatures and timers can be set from the Traeger app rather than at the grill itself. Super Smoke mode raises smoke output on demand.
The cooking chamber measures 3,976 square centimeters and works between 74 and 260 degrees Celsius, covering low smoking through roasting and searing. Dual-wall insulation steadies that heat in cold weather. The hopper takes 10 kg of pellets, grease and ash collect in one EZ-Clean keg, and the P.A.L. rail carries accessories. The grill is 150 cm wide, 64 cm deep, 122 cm tall and weighs 90.5 kg.

excerpt: The 650 pairs app-controlled pellet cooking with 4,232 square centimeters of grate space and a double-wall insulated chamber.
description:
Model TFB65BLFC burns wood pellets and is managed from a digital touchscreen or, remotely, the Traeger app over WiFIRE. Temperature, timers and Super Smoke mode are all handled the same way, whether the cook is standing at the grill or across town.
Grate space totals 4,232 square centimeters, enough for a large roast and side dishes at once. Double-wall construction holds heat through long cooks and trims pellet use. The P.A.L. Pop-And-Lock rail accepts Traeger accessories along the side, and the EZ-Clean keg gathers grease and ash into a single container for emptying.

excerpt: A larger Ironwood with 5,651 square centimeters of cooking area, WiFIRE app control and a double-wall insulated barrel.
description:
This is the roomier Ironwood, model TFB89BLFC, with 5,651 square centimeters of cooking area across its grates. That is enough space to cook for a crowd without working in batches or juggling trays.
Heat is managed from a touchscreen panel, and WiFIRE brings the same controls, timers and recipe library to a phone. Super Smoke mode adds smoke output for cuts that benefit from a longer, cooler stretch. The chamber is double-walled for steadier temperatures and better fuel efficiency, the P.A.L. rail carries accessories, and grease and ash empty from one EZ-Clean keg.

excerpt: Extra-large Ironwood with 5,961 square centimeters of grate space, interior lighting and WiFIRE control from the Traeger app.
description:
Model TFB93RLGI is the widest grill in the Ironwood line at 178 centimeters across, with 5,961 square centimeters of cooking area inside a fully insulated dual-wall chamber. Interior lighting makes the grates readable after dark.
The controller is a touchscreen, and WiFIRE connects it to the Traeger app for remote adjustment and monitoring. Working range runs from 74 to 260 degrees Celsius, and the hopper holds 10 kg of pellets. Depth is 64 centimeters, height 122 centimeters, and the grill weighs 110 kg. Grease and ash collect in the EZ-Clean keg, and the P.A.L. rail takes trays, hooks and bins.

excerpt: Blue-finished Pro series pellet grill with D2 Direct Drive, WiFIRE app control and 3,150 square centimeters of grate space.
description:
The Pro 22 is Traeger's entry point into app-connected pellet cooking, finished in blue. D2 Direct Drive shortens start-up and holds a set temperature steadily, while the digital controller covers adjustments made at the grill.
WiFIRE moves those same controls to a phone, including timers and notifications, and Super Smoke mode increases smoke output for longer cooks. Cooking area totals 3,150 square centimeters, which suits weeknight dinners and small gatherings rather than catering runs. The EZ-Clean grease management system keeps maintenance down to a short routine after cooking.

excerpt: The Pro 575 offers 3,850 square centimeters of cooking area, D2 Direct Drive and wheels for moving it around a patio.
description:
Grate space on the 575 comes to 3,850 square centimeters, a step up for households that cook large roasts or feed a full table regularly. D2 Direct Drive brings the grill up to temperature quickly and keeps it there through a long smoke.
The digital controller covers temperature and timing, and WiFIRE extends both to the Traeger app, with notifications as a cook progresses. Super Smoke mode is a single button. All-terrain wheels let the grill be repositioned around a yard or patio, and the EZ-Clean system manages grease and ash between sessions.

excerpt: The largest Pro model, with 5,543 square centimeters of cooking area and all-terrain wheels for moving it into position.
description:
At 5,543 square centimeters, the 780 has the most grate space in the Pro line, which leaves room for low-and-slow cuts on one side and quicker items on the other. D2 Direct Drive handles start-up and holds temperature once a target is set.
Setpoints are entered on the digital controller or through the Traeger app over WiFIRE, with alerts sent as a cook progresses, and Super Smoke mode raises smoke output when more wood flavor is wanted. Rugged wheels make the grill easy to reposition, and the EZ-Clean grease management system simplifies upkeep.

excerpt: Portable pellet grill with a 184 square inch grate, an 8 lb hopper and a latching lid, built to travel and cook off-site.
description:
The Ranger is the portable member of the Traeger range, sized for tailgates, campsites and small patios. Its grilling area measures 184 square inches and the built-in hopper holds 8 lb of pellets, which covers a long cook without a refill.
The ARC controller sets temperature in five-degree increments and includes a cook timer plus a keep warm mode for food that has to sit. A meat probe reads internal temperature without opening the lid, a cast iron plate is included for griddle work, and baffled lid latches hold everything shut in transit.

excerpt: Model TBB86RLGI adds an induction side cooktop and Smart Combustion control to a 5,677 square centimeter pellet grill.
description:
Traeger's Timberline, model TBB86RLGI, uses Smart Combustion technology to keep temperatures even across the chamber, with dual-wall insulated steel around it for stability in cold or windy conditions. An induction cooktop is built into the side for searing, sauteing or holding a pot of sauce.
Cooking area measures 5,677 square centimeters and the working range runs from 74 to 260 degrees Celsius. The pellet hopper holds 9.98 kg. Controls sit on a touchscreen and travel to the Traeger app over WiFIRE, Super Smoke mode boosts smoke output, and the cabinet is rated for built-in installation in an outdoor kitchen.

excerpt: Top of the Timberline line: 8,516 square centimeters of cooking area, an induction side burner and built-in ready cabinetry.
description:
The XL carries 8,516 square centimeters of cooking area, the largest in the Timberline line, managed by Smart Combustion technology that holds an accurate temperature through a long smoke or a hot sear. Insulated dual-wall steel keeps that performance consistent in poor weather.
A side induction cooktop handles searing and simmering alongside the main chamber. The Downdraft Exhaust system works with Super Smoke mode to circulate smoke around the food, and the touchscreen and Traeger app share the same controls over WiFIRE. Grease and ash empty from a single keg, and the cabinet is designed to be built into an outdoor kitchen.

excerpt: Four-post storage and service lift rated at 9,000 lbs, with extra-long runways, 15 lock positions and a 110V supply.
description:
This four-post lift is rated at 9,000 lbs and built longer and taller than a standard storage model, so full-size trucks and SUVs fit on the runways with a second vehicle parked underneath. It runs on 110V and requires no permanent anchoring, which keeps it practical in a garage that may be rearranged later.
An outside slider design carries the load, automatic safety locks engage at 15 positions, and a single-point release lowers the lift. Drip trays shield whatever is parked below. A caster kit and jack tray are included. Coverage runs one year on parts and 30 days on hydraulics, with a seal kit provided afterward.

excerpt: Zero-turn with a 24 HP Kohler twin, a 50-inch twin-blade deck and a tubular steel frame under a limited lifetime warranty.
description:
Power on the Mustang Z50 comes from a 725cc Kohler twin-cylinder rated at 24 HP, paired with dual hydrostatic transmissions and lap bar steering for genuine zero-turn movement around trees and beds. The lap bars also carry an integrated parking brake.
The 50-inch twin-blade deck rides on two anti-scalp wheels and a nose roller that keep the blades off high spots in the turf, and a deck wash port takes a garden hose for rinsing clippings from underneath. The frame is fully welded 2-inch tubular steel, covered by a limited lifetime warranty. A rear bagger or mulch kit can be added separately.

excerpt: Wide-deck walk-behind with 195cc Troy-Bilt power, rear-wheel drive that matches walking pace, and a three-year warranty.
description:
Model TBWC28T cuts a 28-inch path from a steel deck, wider than most walk-behind mowers, which reduces the number of passes needed on an open lawn. The 195cc Troy-Bilt overhead valve engine starts easily and runs quieter than older designs.
InStep variable-speed rear-wheel drive adjusts to walking pace and keeps traction on uneven ground, helped by 8-inch front and 13-inch rear wheels. Clippings can be side discharged, mulched or rear bagged, and deck height changes through a single lever. A deck wash port accepts a garden hose. The mower arrives fully assembled with a three-year limited warranty.

excerpt: Self-propelled mower with a 28-inch steel deck, single-lever height control and a choice of bagging, mulching or discharge.
description:
Three ways of handling clippings are built into this Troy-Bilt walk-behind: side discharge for tall growth, mulching to return nutrients to the lawn, and a rear bag for a clean finish. A single lever moves the deck between cutting heights.
The deck itself is steel and 28 inches wide, driven by a 195cc Troy-Bilt overhead valve engine. InStep variable-speed rear-wheel drive matches the operator's pace on slopes and rough ground, with 8-inch front and 13-inch rear wheels underneath. The TBWC28T ships fully assembled, includes a deck wash port for hose cleaning, and carries a three-year limited warranty.

excerpt: Riding tractor with a 19HP Briggs and Stratton Intek, a 42-inch twin-blade deck and car-style foot pedal drive control.
description:
The Bronco 42 runs a 540CC Briggs and Stratton Intek engine rated at 19HP with pressure lubrication, and drives through an AutoDrive transmission where a single foot pedal sets both speed and direction, much like a car.
Its twin-blade deck cuts 42 inches wide and adjusts across five positions, with anti-scalp wheels keeping the blades clear of uneven turf. An 18-inch turn radius helps around trees and flower beds. The Step-Thru frame opens up legroom and makes mounting easier, the seat is mid-back, and rubber footpads cut vibration. A rear hitch takes a bagger, mulch kit, dump cart or aerator, sold separately.

excerpt: Battery riding tractor running a 56V MAX 60Ah pack, with a 42-inch deck and twelve cutting heights between 1 and 4 inches.
description:
Nothing here needs fuel or oil changes: a 56V MAX 60Ah lithium-ion pack drives a brushless motor, and Troy-Bilt rates the machine for up to 1.5 hours of mowing, or about two acres, per charge. Running noise sits up to 65 percent below a comparable gas mower.
The twin-blade deck cuts 42 inches wide, with dual anti-scalp wheels and twelve height settings from 1 to 4 inches. Speed is set by foot pedal, and cruise control holds a pace on long straight runs. The front axle is cast iron, the frame is Step-Thru for easier mounting, and the high-back seat adjusts.

excerpt: Electric riding mower with cruise control, a cast iron front axle and up to 1.5 hours of mowing from a single charge.
description:
The 42E XP replaces the gas engine with a 56V MAX 60Ah lithium-ion battery and a brushless electric motor, which takes oil changes and fuel off the maintenance list and drops operating noise by up to 65 percent against a gas machine.
One charge covers roughly two acres, or about 1.5 hours of mowing. The 42-inch twin-blade deck offers twelve cutting heights between 1 and 4 inches and rides on dual anti-scalp wheels. Foot-pedal speed control and cruise control handle the driving, while a cast iron front axle, Step-Thru frame and adjustable high-back seat cover stability and comfort. The rear hitch tows spreaders and aerators.

excerpt: Deluxe Series four-post lift rated at 8,000 lbs, with multiple lock positions, built-in drip trays and a powder-coated finish.
description:
Rated at 8,000 lbs, this Deluxe Series four-post lift suits both storage and service work, holding cars, SUVs and light-duty trucks on reinforced steel posts. Stacked parking doubles what a single bay holds, which matters in a tight home garage or a collector's space.
Mechanical locks engage at several heights, so the runways can sit wherever a job needs them, and a single-point release drops all four posts together. Built-in drip trays catch fluid before it reaches the vehicle below, and the powder-coated finish resists rust and everyday shop wear.

excerpt: A 1.8-ton mini excavator supplied with twelve attachments, retractable tracks, a swing boom and a Kubota D722 diesel.
description:
Twelve attachments ship with this 1.8-ton excavator: a 415mm bucket, a 600mm tilting bucket, a 200mm trencher, a 500mm grader, a concrete breaker, ripper, rake, auger, grappler, screening bucket, hydraulic thumb and quick hitch. That covers digging, demolition, sorting and grading from one machine.
The Kubota D722 is a 16.4HP water-cooled diesel meeting Tier 4. Tracks retract to pass through gates and orchard rows, and the swing boom deflects 55 degrees left and 45 degrees right for work along fences and pipes. Dig depth is 2100mm, dig height 3080mm, bucket capacity 0.04 cbm, and the 840mm swing radius gives zero tail swing.

excerpt: Four-ton class mini excavator with a Kubota D1703 diesel, boom swing and a climate-controlled cabin with LED lighting.
description:
The KUVOU 4.0 sits in the four-ton class and is built for trenching, foundation work, landscaping and material handling on sites where a full-size machine cannot turn. It measures 5029 mm long, 1554 mm wide and 2580 mm tall, with a 1720 mm top width and 2150 mm track length on 300 mm standard shoes.
Digging force at the bucket is 30.4 kN, with 18.2 kN at the boom, which suits compacted ground and hard dirt. Boom swing lets an operator work close to walls and corners without repositioning the machine. The Kubota D1703 diesel supplies the power, and the cabin has climate control and LED lighting for early starts and late finishes.

excerpt: Mini skid steer weighing 1,800 lbs, powered by a 21hp Honda GX630 and driving through hydraulic four-wheel drive.
description:
Built for jobs where a full-size loader will not fit, this 1,800 lb machine works comfortably in gardens, orchards, parks and narrow lots. The Honda GX630 produces 21hp with maximum torque of 48.3 NM at 2500 rpm, and drive is hydraulic to all four wheels.
Typical work runs from digging, drilling and grabbing to dozing, ditch cleaning, rock breaking and general landscaping. The controls are straightforward enough for someone running a loader for the first time. A standard digging bucket, a tool box and a digital manual are included with the machine.

excerpt: Compact skid-steer loader with a 22.1HP Honda GX690 V-Twin, 830 lb lift capacity and a three-valve hydraulic system.
description:
At 1,830 lbs, this STOMP loader is sized for orchards, barns and urban lots where standard equipment cannot get through the access. The Honda GX690 V-Twin is a four-stroke petrol engine rated at 22.1HP with 48.3NM of torque.
Lift capacity is 830 lbs and travel speed reaches 5.5 kph, with hydraulic drive to all four wheels for traction on slopes and soft ground. A three-valve auxiliary hydraulic system runs standard skid-steer attachments, augers, grapples and brooms among them. A standard digging bucket, a heavy-duty toolbox and a digital operation manual come with it.

excerpt: A 1.4-ton mini skid steer with a Kubota D1105 diesel, pilot controls and a 360-degree pivot for working in tight quarters.
description:
The STOMP 509 is a 1.4-ton loader for construction, landscaping, road maintenance and airport work, narrow enough for gates, low-ceiling spaces and paths where larger loaders stop. A zero-turn 360-degree pivot keeps it working in place rather than shuffling back and forth.
The Kubota D1105 is a water-cooled diesel rated at 25HP at 3000 RPM and 19HP at 2200 RPM. Operating weight is 1.4 tons and transport length with the bucket fitted is 2570 mm. The cabin is 700 mm wide with pilot controls, and the front-mounted bucket handles digging, grading, material handling, demolition and snow removal.

excerpt: Stand-on track loader measuring 35.9 inches wide, with a Kubota D1105 diesel and dual auxiliary hydraulic circuits.
description:
A chassis just 35.9 inches across is the point of the V900: it clears standard gates and interior doorways while still working at a 1.4-ton operating weight. The Kubota D1105 is a three-cylinder water-cooled diesel of 1,226 cc rated at 25HP, producing 71.5 newton meters of peak torque, and it meets EPA and EU Stage V.
Hydraulics run three pumps and three valves at 48 L/min and 16 MPa, with a dual auxiliary circuit for attachments needing independent functions. A separate oil cooler holds temperatures during continuous cycles. Rated operating capacity is 1,014 lbs, maximum load 1,102 lbs, dumping height 5.6 feet, and the fuel tank takes 33 litres.

excerpt: Stand-on skid steer with a dual auxiliary hydraulic system, 1,014 lb rated capacity and a 1,226 cc Kubota diesel.
description:
Most mini track loaders offer a single auxiliary circuit. This one carries a dual auxiliary output fed by a three-pump, three-valve system delivering 12.7 GPM at 2,321 PSI, so implements with independent functions such as swing or side-shift can be run properly. Quick-connect couplers speed up changes, and an independent oil cooler keeps the system stable.
The Kubota D1105 three-cylinder diesel displaces 1,226 cc, makes 25HP and 71.5 newton meters of torque, and draws from an 8.7-gallon tank. Rated operating capacity is 1,014 lbs with a maximum load of 1,102 lbs, and the machine is 35.9 inches wide at a 1.4-ton operating weight.

excerpt: Compact stand-on loader for fleet work, with EPA and Stage V diesel power and a 9.4-foot maximum operating height.
description:
For contractors and rental yards, the V900 covers work that full-size machines cannot reach. It measures 35.9 inches across, fits through standard gates and backyard access, and carries a 1.4-ton operating weight that keeps it planted under load.
The Kubota D1105 three-cylinder water-cooled diesel supplies 25HP and meets EPA and EU Stage V requirements. Hydraulics deliver 48 L/min at 16 MPa through a three-pump, three-valve layout, with a dual auxiliary circuit for multi-function attachments that single-circuit loaders cannot operate. Rated operating capacity is 1,014 lbs, maximum load 1,102 lbs, and maximum operating height 9.4 feet.

excerpt: Wheeled mini loader that clears a 36-inch gate, lifts 830 lbs and runs attachments from three hydraulic valves.
description:
Width decides many jobs, and this wheeled STOMP passes through a 36-inch gate, which puts it to work in orchards, barns and fenced backyards. Operating weight is 1,830 lbs and lift capacity 830 lbs, close to half the machine's own weight.
The Honda GX690 V-Twin produces 22.1HP with 48.3NM of torque. Hydraulic four-wheel drive supplies traction on slopes and mud at speeds up to 5.5 kph, and three auxiliary valves let it run augers, grapples, trenchers and similar tools. It is supplied with a standard digging bucket, a heavy-duty toolbox and a digital operator manual.

excerpt: A 1.1-ton cabin excavator with a 380mm bucket, a hydraulic thumb clip and an oil cooler for longer working sessions.
description:
At 1.1 tons, the TERROR ONE is a small excavator meant for gardens, parks, farmyards and roadside work where access is the limiting factor. The 13.5hp Briggs and Stratton engine keeps servicing simple.
The bucket measures 380mm across and holds 0.022 cbm, and a hydraulic thumb clip lets the operator grab brush, rock and debris rather than only scooping. A hydraulic oil cooler and fan hold temperatures down through longer digging sessions. Typical tasks run from trenching and ditch cleaning to drilling, rock breaking and light dozing, all from an enclosed cabin.

excerpt: A one-ton trench digger running a Briggs & Stratton XR2100 engine, with an oil cooler, canopy and thumb clip fitted.
description:
Typhon built this machine for ground where a full-size excavator has nowhere to sit: orchard rows, fenced yards, garden beds and small municipal sites. A 13.5 hp Briggs & Stratton XR2100 engine drives it, and a hydraulic oil cooler keeps oil temperatures in check through a long afternoon of digging.
The 380 mm bucket holds 0.022 cbm and reaches a digging depth of 1,725 mm, with 405 mm of platform ground clearance and a maximum machine height of 2,490 mm. Front turning radius tops out at 1,490 mm. The canopy and hydraulic thumb clip are fitted from the start, so handling rock, pipe and brush calls for no added attachment.

excerpt: One-ton Typhon excavator with a 13.5 HP Briggs & Stratton gas engine, hydraulic oil cooler, canopy, bucket and thumb clip.
description:
Garden plots, farm lanes and park paths rarely leave room for full-size equipment. This one-ton machine works in that gap, and the upper body turns a full 360 degrees, so spoil can be placed without repositioning the tracks each time.
