excerpt: A 4,000 lb Kubota D902 mini excavator with a 450mm bucket and an included hydraulic thumb, compact enough for doorways.
description:
Four thousand pounds of excavator with a Kubota D902 under the hood, EPA certified to Tier 4. Tank capacities are 20.5 liters of hydraulic oil and 13.5 liters of diesel, which keeps the machine working through a long stretch without a stop to refill.
The 450mm bucket moves 0.025 cubic meters at a time, sized for trenching between rows or along a foundation, and a hydraulic thumb clip is included for handling pipe, rock, and debris. Critical components use stainless steel to resist corrosion, and the compact frame fits through a standard doorway or into an elevator for interior work.

excerpt: A 1.8-ton mini excavator on Kubota D902 power, with a 0.025 cbm bucket, stainless components, and elevator-friendly dimensions.
description:
A compact excavator at 4,000 lbs operating weight, powered by the EPA-certified Kubota D902 and plumbed with a 20.5 liter hydraulic reservoir alongside a 13.5 liter diesel tank.
It carries a 450mm bucket with a 0.025 cubic meter capacity, well matched to orchard trenching, basement digs, and finish landscaping where a larger machine would do damage. A hydraulic thumb comes with it for gripping material, stainless steel protects critical components against corrosion, and the frame passes through standard doorways and elevators for interior access.

excerpt: A 1.8-ton mini excavator with a heated and air-conditioned cabin, dual-pump hydraulics, and a 400mm standard bucket.
description:
The cabin is the difference here, an enclosed operator station with air conditioning and heat, so the machine stays workable through a cold morning or a hot afternoon. Operating weight is 4,000 lbs, and the engine is a Kubota D902 that meets Tier 4 and carries EPA certification.
A dual-pump hydraulic system with double throttle valve technology runs two attachments at the same time without a drop in pressure, so a thumb and an auger can work together. The standard bucket is 400mm, sized for root pruning, irrigation trenching, and planting between rows. Stainless steel joints resist corrosion.

excerpt: A remote-controlled 5,000 lb car lift with several locking height positions and no permanent floor installation required.
description:
Rated at 5,000 lb and run from a handheld remote, so raising and lowering happens without anyone working a control at the base. Height adjusts across several positions, which lets the same unit suit a low car and a taller light-duty truck.
The frame is steel with reinforced lifting arms, and an automatic locking system catches at each height position rather than relying on hydraulic pressure alone. Nothing needs to be bolted into the slab, which keeps it practical for a home garage, a detailing bay, or a small repair shop where the floor has other uses.

excerpt: A portable 5,000 lb car lift operated by remote, with adjustable working heights and automatic locks at each position.
description:
Lifting a car at home usually means giving up floor space to a permanent installation. This one avoids that. It is a 5,000 lb capacity unit that sits on the slab without anchoring, moves when it needs to, and is operated by remote control.
Several height settings cover brake work, tire rotation, fluid changes, and detailing underneath, and an automatic lock engages at each position while the vehicle is up. Construction is heavy-gauge steel with reinforced arms, rated for sedans, coupes, and light-duty trucks.

excerpt: A 6,000 lb low-rise lift on UHMW rollers with a tow handle, collapsing to four inches for low-clearance vehicles.
description:
The portable take on a low-rise lift. High-density UHMW rollers and a tow handle let one person move it between bays instead of committing a bay to it, and the rollers are hard enough that they do not wear out in service. Capacity is 6,000 lb, covering light-duty trucks, SUVs, and cars.
It collapses to four inches, low enough to slide under a car with little ground clearance, and the electric/hydraulic power unit raises it onto multi-position locks. A single-point release drops both locks together for an even descent. Rubber lifting blocks are included and the frame is heavy steel channel.

excerpt: A compact 6,000 lb scissor lift running on 110V, with 23.5 inches of rise and multi-position safety locks.
description:
Quick-service work such as wheels, brakes, and body repair does not need a vehicle up at head height, and this scissor lift keeps it low. Rated at 6,000 lb, it starts at four inches and rises to 23.5 inches, driven by a 110V electric/hydraulic power unit.
Safety locks hold at multiple points through the travel, and the crossbar is dropped so the underside stays reachable. The steel channel frame takes up 83 by 74 inches of floor, narrow enough for a tight bay, and rubber lifting blocks are included for contact with the vehicle frame.

excerpt: A portable mid-rise scissor lift rated at 6,000 lb, reaching 42.25 inches with adjustable arms and a wheeled power unit.
description:
A mid-rise scissor lift that brings a vehicle to working height for wheel, brake, and suspension jobs without filling the bay. Travel runs from 4.75 inches collapsed to 42.25 inches raised, on a footprint of 93 by 45 inches, with 110V power.
The power unit rides on a cart, so the lift moves from bay to bay rather than staying put. Adjustable arm assemblies set the contact points for a given vehicle, a multi-position lock bar holds the chosen height, and solid steel frame support bars carry the 6,000 lb rating. Truck adapters are included.

excerpt: A mid-rise open-center lift rated at 6,000 lb, with equalizing hydraulics, automatic lock bars, and removable approach ramps.
description:
An open center means nothing runs down the middle of the lift, so the exhaust, driveline, and floorpan stay accessible while the car is up. Longer platforms and a wide spread between lift points take in vehicles with long wheelbases as well as ordinary cars.
The load rating is 6,000 lb, carried on four steel scissor bars, solid through their section, with a dual master hydraulic cylinder and equalizing cylinders keeping both sides level. Steel lock bars engage automatically on the way up and release together at the push of a button. The approach ramps lift out for a flush-mount installation.

excerpt: A 7,000 lb remote-operated car lift with multiple locking heights, reinforced steel arms, and no permanent installation.
description:
Seven thousand pounds of capacity puts SUVs and light-duty trucks in range, not just cars, and the whole unit runs from a remote rather than a control at the base. Height adjusts across several positions to suit a low sports car or a taller pickup.
Steel construction with reinforced lifting arms handles repeated use, and the automatic locking system engages at each height position. No slab anchoring is required, so the lift can be positioned for a job and moved aside afterward, which works for a home garage, a mobile operation, or a small shop.

excerpt: An ALI-certified 8,000 lb four-post lift for home garages and restorations, with a caster kit, drip trays, and wheel stops.
description:
A four-post lift aimed at home garages and restoration shops rather than production bays, ALI certified and rated at 8,000 lb. The extended length suits longer vehicles, and stacking one passenger car over another doubles what a single space holds.
It is built heavier than comparable lifts, roughly 200 lbs more, with a lock ladder design, a double lock safety system, and a single-point release. Steel approach ramps, drip trays, four wheel stops, and a caster kit with polyurethane wheels come with it, so it rolls to a new spot. Anchor bolts are optional for a fixed installation.

excerpt: A one-burner portable Weber that folds down with a single hand and still offers about 2,065 sq cm of cast iron grate space.
description:
Weber built this portable around a single stainless steel burner and a cooking surface of roughly 63 by 34 cm, about 2,065 sq cm, which is enough room to feed four people. Porcelain-enameled cast iron grates hold heat for searing, and a lid thermometer lets you follow the temperature without opening the hood.
The cart folds with one hand and rolls on all-weather wheels, collapsing to 94 cm high by 58 wide and 34 deep for a trunk or a tight corner of the garage. Open, it stands 111 cm tall. A side table with tool hooks handles prep, and the burner runs on a butane or propane cartridge. Weight is roughly 22 kg.

excerpt: Black-finished portable Weber with a 13,000 BTU burner, an automatic lid lock, and a trolley that opens and folds one-handed.
description:
Finished in black, this Traveler runs a single high-performance stainless steel front burner rated at 13,000 BTU per hour, or 3.81 kW, over a 63.5 by 34.3 cm porcelain-enameled cast iron grate. That is room for about 15 burgers or 20 sausages at once, so nobody waits for a second round.
The scissor trolley stands up and folds with one hand, and the lid lock engages on its own as the grill closes. Two heavy-duty wheels handle rough ground, and a side table with three tool holders keeps utensils within reach. A grease management system and a thermometer in the shroud are standard. Regulator and hose are included, and Weber covers it with a five-year limited warranty.

excerpt: A two-burner Weber Q on a fixed cart, with a taller lid for roasting larger cuts and fold-down side tables on both sides.
description:
Two stainless steel burners with separate control knobs let you set a hot zone and a cooler one across a cooking surface of roughly 54 by 39 cm. The porcelain-enameled cast iron grates hold steady heat, and the raised lid leaves headroom for roasting a larger cut with the hood down.
The permanent cart brings the grill to a comfortable working height and adds a lower shelf and tool hooks. Both side tables fold away when they are not needed, and the drip tray pulls out for cleaning. Ignition is push-button, a thermometer sits in the lid, and a regulator is included for butane or propane cylinders. It measures 126 cm wide by 66 deep and 120 tall, at about 27 kg.

excerpt: Three-burner freestanding flat top with a pre-seasoned carbon steel cooktop and a closed cabinet base for tool storage.
description:
A flat top for cooks who want more than a grate outdoors. The pre-seasoned carbon steel surface measures 76 by 27 cm, around 2,052 sq cm, and three stainless steel burners sit beneath it so heat stays even from one end to the other. Electronic ignition and individual control knobs handle startup and zoning.
The closed cabinet base hides tools and accessories, and a side table gives you somewhere to set plates and prep bowls. Grease drains to a tray that pulls out from the front, and tool hooks keep spatulas at hand. A lid protects the cooktop between sessions. The unit stands 101.5 cm tall, 132 cm wide and 62 cm deep, weighing about 52.4 kg.

excerpt: Compact two-burner gas grill with flavorizer bars, fold-down side tables, and an enclosed cart that hides the gas bottle.
description:
Two stainless steel burners heat a 52 by 45 cm cooking area, with porcelain-enameled flavorizer bars set between the burners and the porcelain-enameled cast iron grates. Electronic ignition gets things going quickly, and a thermometer in the lid tracks the temperature inside.
Both side tables fold down when space is tight, which matters on a patio or a balcony. The cart encloses the gas bottle behind a front panel, carries integrated tool hooks, and rolls on two wheels. With the lid closed it measures 113 cm tall by 127 wide and 63 deep; open, the lid raises overall height to 160 cm. Weight is about 45 kg, and it runs on propane or butane.

excerpt: Four-post hydraulic lift rated for 8,500 pounds, with a rolling caster kit and extra-wide runways for longer vehicles.
description:
Rated at 8,500 pounds, this four-post lift handles cars, SUVs and light-duty trucks, whether the job is stacking two vehicles in a home garage or raising one for service. The four-post layout spreads the load and keeps the platform steady while you work underneath.
A caster kit is built in, so the lift can be rolled to a different spot when the garage layout changes. Lowering runs through a single-point lock release, with several secure lock positions along the travel. The runways are extra wide to suit long-wheelbase vehicles and modern SUVs, and the powder-coated steel resists corrosion, leaving little routine upkeep beyond the hydraulics.

excerpt: A 20,000-running-watt Westinghouse with a 999 cc V-twin engine, electric start, and transfer-switch-ready outlets.
description:
Twenty thousand running watts, with 28,000 available at peak, puts this unit in home backup and job site territory rather than tailgate duty. A 999 cc V-twin OHV Westinghouse engine drives it, and the 17.17-gallon tank supports up to 17 hours of running at 25 percent load. Starting is push-button electric.
Transfer-switch-ready L14-30R and 14-50R outlets connect it to a house panel or heavy equipment, and total harmonic distortion stays under 5 percent, so sensitive electronics can be charged straight from the control panel. A built-in carbon monoxide sensor watches exhaust levels. The steel frame carries heavy-duty wheels and handles, and coverage is a three-year limited warranty with lifetime technical support.

excerpt: Ultra-duty 28,000-peak-watt generator with a carbon monoxide sensor, lift brackets, and a real-time performance display.
description:
Built around a 999 cc V-twin OHV engine, this generator produces 20,000 running watts and 28,000 at peak, drawing from a 17.17-gallon tank with a fuel gauge that supports up to 17 hours at 25 percent load. The start panel groups the push-button starter, choke knob and fuel control valve in one place.
Outlets cover four GFCI 120V 5-20R household receptacles, two 50-amp 120/240V 14-50R connections and 30-amp 120/240V twist-lock outlets, all transfer-switch ready and holding under 5 percent THD. A VFT data center shows real-time performance information for maintenance planning, and a carbon monoxide sensor monitors the exhaust. The steel frame adds lift brackets alongside the wheel and handle kit. Warranty is three years limited.

excerpt: Compact 592 Wh power station with a pure sine wave inverter, AC, USB and DC outputs, and a readout for remaining charge.
description:
A 592 Wh battery and a pure sine wave inverter rated at roughly 1,000 running watts, 1,200 at peak, make this a sensible stopgap when the lights go out and an easy thing to bring to a campsite. Clean output means laptops and other sensitive electronics can be plugged in directly.
The panel combines standard AC outlets, USB ports and a DC port, so a phone, a light and a laptop can draw at the same time. A digital display reports battery level, input and output status and runtime, which makes it simple to judge how much is left. The case is light enough to carry in one hand and to store on a shelf between uses.

excerpt: Portable power station that refills from AC, solar or a car socket, with an RV outlet, wireless charging and an LED light.
description:
Three charging paths keep this unit topped up: a wall outlet at home, solar panels when you are off grid, and a vehicle 12V socket on the road. That flexibility is the point, since a power station is only worth carrying if it can be refilled wherever you end up.
The panel carries AC outlets, USB ports and DC connections, plus an RV plug and a wireless charging pad, so several devices can run or charge together. A control screen reports battery status, power output and runtime while the unit works, and a built-in LED light helps during an outage. A Bluetooth speaker and Wi-Fi connection are included as well.

excerpt: Solid-state power station holding 2,611 Wh, with 4,000 W of continuous output and eleven ways to connect a device.
description:
Solid-state cells are the reason this one is worth a look: they take up less room and weigh less than conventional lithium-ion, which is how 2,611 Wh and a 4,000 W continuous inverter fit into a 53.6 lb case. Peak output reaches 6,000 W, enough for a refrigerator or a corded power tool.
Ten ports on the control panel cover AC, DC, USB-A and USB-C, and two 15-watt wireless pads on the top surface bring the total to eleven connections. Recharging takes about 90 minutes from a wall outlet, 5.5 hours from solar, or 22 hours from a car. App control over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth is supported, and Smart Link ties in extra batteries when you need more reserve.

excerpt: A 53.6-pound backup battery that runs refrigerators and power tools, and refills from a wall outlet in about 90 minutes.
description:
Rated at 4,000 W continuous and 6,000 W at peak, with 2,611 Wh of storage, this station covers a refrigerator, power tools and household electronics through an outage. The solid-state battery keeps the whole thing at 53.6 pounds, light enough for one person to move it to a truck bed or an RV.
It refills from a wall outlet in roughly 90 minutes, from solar in about 5.5 hours, or from a car socket over 22 hours. The control panel holds ten ports, including AC, DC, USB-A and USB-C, with two 15-watt wireless charging pads on top. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth app control handle monitoring, and Smart Link adds batteries as needs grow. It runs with no gas and no fumes.

excerpt: Quiet, fume-free 2,611 Wh battery station with a 100 W USB-C PD port, wireless pads and Smart Link capacity expansion.
description:
What a solid-state pack leaves out is the appeal: no gas, no fumes, no engine noise, and 53.6 pounds to carry. Storage is 2,611 Wh, and the inverter supplies 4,000 W continuously with 6,000 W on tap for startup surges, which covers most home devices including a refrigerator.
Eleven connections are available in total. Ten ports on the control panel span AC, DC, RV, USB-A and USB-C, including a 100 W Type-C PD port, and two 15-watt wireless pads sit on top. An LED light is built in. Charge from AC in about 90 minutes, from solar in 5.5 hours, or from a vehicle in 22 hours, and use Smart Link to stack more batteries for larger backup jobs.

excerpt: Kubota-powered 3,800 lb mini excavator with dual auxiliary hydraulic circuits, pilot joystick controls and a hydraulic thumb.
description:
A 3,800-pound machine with an EPA-certified Kubota D902 three-cylinder diesel behind the cab, producing 15.8 horsepower at 2,200 rpm and up to 20.4 horsepower at 3,600 rpm when a hard pass calls for it. The 3.17-gallon fuel tank and 4.76-gallon hydraulic oil reservoir stretch the time between refills.
Hydraulics operate at 18 MPa, about 2,611 psi, with a 1.82 GPM pilot flow behind the joysticks for steady control during fine grading and trenching. Double-sided auxiliary throttle valves feed two attachment circuits at once, so a hydraulic thumb can work alongside another powered attachment. Digging depth reaches 86 inches.

excerpt: Forty-two-inch zero-turn with a 20 HP gas engine and dual hydrostatic drive for tight turns around trees and beds.
description:
A 20 horsepower gas engine and dual hydrostatic transmissions give this zero-turn the agility to pivot around trees, beds and fence posts instead of backing up for a second pass. The 42-inch cutting width suits yards where a wider machine would be awkward to steer.
Cutting height adjusts to match the season, and the deck can be set for mulching, bagging or rear discharge depending on what the lawn needs that week. The operator station keeps the controls straightforward and the seat adjustable for longer sessions. Service points are easy to reach, which keeps routine maintenance from turning into an afternoon project.

excerpt: A 21.5 HP V-twin zero-turn with a 42-inch Accel Deep deck, LED lighting and a high-back seat with armrests.
description:
The 21.5 horsepower V-twin holds its speed through thick grass, and the 42-inch Accel Deep deck is built to cut cleanly at the higher end of the mowing range. Deck height sets from 1.25 to 4.5 inches using a foot lift with an adjustment dial, and the deck accepts a bagging or mulching setup.
Dual EZT transmissions and 18-inch drive tires carry it to 7 mph, with the park brake engaging as soon as the steering levers swing outward. The 20-inch high-back seat adjusts and has armrests, the motion control levers move to fit the operator, and tracking can be corrected from the seat. LED lights help at dusk. Floor mats, covered tool storage, a removable foot platform for deck cleaning and a 3-gallon tank round it out.

excerpt: Forty-eight-inch forged Accel Deep deck and a 24 HP V-twin, with an automatic park brake and seat-side tracking adjustment.
description:
Twenty-four horsepower from a V-twin engine, paired with a 48-inch forged Accel Deep deck, moves this zero-turn across a larger property without trading cut quality for ground speed. Deck height runs from 1.25 to 4.5 inches, set with the foot lift, and the deck converts to bag or mulch.
Dual EZT transmissions and 18-inch drive tires take it up to 7 mph, and the park brake engages on its own when the steering levers swing outward. The 18-inch high-back seat and the motion control levers both adjust, and tracking can be trued up without leaving the seat. A PowerFlow bagger, mulch control kit and hitch are sold separately. The three-year bumper-to-bumper warranty is worth registering after delivery.

excerpt: Wide-deck zero-turn pairing a 54-inch forged cutting deck with a 24 HP V-twin and mowing speeds of up to 7 mph.
description:
The 54-inch forged Accel Deep deck covers more ground per pass, and the 24 horsepower V-twin keeps the blades turning at speed in heavy grass. Cutting heights run from 1.25 to 4.5 inches, set with a foot lift, and the deck converts for bagging or mulching.
Dual EZT transmissions push mowing speeds to 7 mph on 18-inch drive tires, while a tougher frame and larger front tires smooth out uneven ground. The 18-inch high-back seat adjusts to the operator, as do the motion control levers, and tracking alignment can be corrected from the seat. Fuel capacity is 3 gallons. Every machine gets a ten-point inspection before sale and carries a three-year warranty.

excerpt: Residential zero-turn with a 60-inch Accel Deep deck, a 24 HP ELS V-twin, foldable ROPS and a 4.5-gallon fuel tank.
description:
Sixty inches of Accel Deep deck is a lot of cut per pass, and the 24 horsepower V-twin ELS engine has the advanced filtration and the output to push it through tall or damp grass. The deck can be fitted for bagging or mulching as the season changes.
The operator station puts a fuel gauge and hour meter in plain view, and the 18-inch seat is cut and sewn over thick foam with armrests for support on long jobs. A foldable rollover protection structure and a retractable seat belt come standard. The 4.5-gallon tank stretches the time between stops. This is a residential ZTrak, aimed at owners who need maneuverability and close trimming around obstacles.

excerpt: Complete two-bag collection system for 54-inch decks, with a PowerFlow blower, chute, hopper and the required ballast weights.
description:
Everything needed to collect clippings off a 54-inch deck arrives together: an attachment bar and hitch, a High-Performance PowerFlow blower, the chute and the hopper assembly. The ballast weights required for safe operation are included, so nothing else has to be ordered.
The blower moves material up the chute without bogging down, and a fill indicator on the chute signals when the bags are getting full. Capacity is 6.5 bushels, roughly 229 liters, split across two bags that lift out for emptying. Standard mower blades work with it, so no blade swap is needed. It fits John Deere Z515E and Z530M machines with a 54-inch deck and measures 51 inches wide, 45 tall and 26 deep.

excerpt: Dual fuel 36-inch range with six sealed Italian burners over an electric convection oven, in a fingerprint-resistant finish.
description:
Gas on top, electricity below. Six sealed Italian hand-cast burners run from 1,000 to 18,000 BTU, covering a low simmer through a hard sear, while the electric convection oven holds an even temperature for baking. Oven capacity is 4.6 cubic feet and takes pans up to 27 inches wide.
The DuraSnow stainless finish resists fingerprints, and the hand-finished porcelain cooktop with its single-piece cast iron grate wipes down in one pass. Inside, triple-layered glass and an aluminum mesh seal hold heat, dual lighting and ball-bearing racks make the cavity easy to work in, and StayPut hinges steady the door. Height adjusts between 36 and 38.5 inches, and an LP conversion kit is included for professional installation.

excerpt: A rear-engine riding mower with a 36-inch steel deck and six-speed gear drive, sized for yards up to an acre.
description:
Rear-engine riders earn their keep on lots where a wide deck simply will not fit. This one puts an 11.5 HP Briggs & Stratton single-cylinder engine behind the seat and a 36-inch reinforced stamped steel deck up front, narrow enough to clear most gates, with a six-speed manual transmission for setting ground speed by hand.
Turf Saver wheels and a turning radius of 18 inches keep it tight around trees and beds. The seat is mid-back, the steering wheel soft-touch, and an LED headlight covers dusk work. A mulching kit ships with it, and coverage runs two years under a limited warranty. Suited to yards up to one acre.

excerpt: Front-engine rider with a 46-inch deck, hydrostatic foot-pedal drive and a 23 HP Kohler twin, built for yards up to two acres.
description:
Two acres is a lot of ground for a push mower, and the T2400 is built for that middle range. A 23 HP Kohler 7000 Series twin-cylinder engine drives a 46-inch reinforced steel deck, and the hydrostatic transmission is worked by foot pedal, so speed changes happen without stopping to shift.
Cutting height adjusts between 1 and 4 inches, and the deck handles side discharge, with bagging and mulching options. Ground speed tops out at 5.5 mph forward and 3 mph in reverse, the fuel tank holds 3 gallons, and a 5-inch Turn Tight radius keeps passes close around obstacles. A front-end bumper, high-back seat and soft-touch steering wheel round it out.

excerpt: A 54-inch stamped steel deck and 24 HP Kohler V-twin put this front-engine rider on properties reaching two acres.
description:
Deck width here is 54 inches of stamped steel, fed by a 24 HP Kohler 7000 Series twin-cylinder engine, which is enough machine for properties running to about two acres. Hydrostatic drive with foot pedal control handles speed and direction, and the 5-inch Turn Tight radius trims the passes needed around trees and posts.
Wheels measure 16 by 6.5 inches in front and 22 by 9.5 inches at the rear for footing on uneven turf. An AGM battery handles starting, the fuel tank holds 3 gallons, and a front-end brush guard takes the knocks. Assembly happens in Martin, Tennessee and Willard, Ohio. A mulching kit is available separately.

excerpt: A steering-wheel zero turn with Synchro-Steer four-wheel control, rated for slopes up to 20 degrees and yards near two acres.
description:
A steering wheel in place of lap bars: Synchro-Steer sends control to all four wheels, which holds a line across hillsides where a conventional zero turn tends to slide. Cub Cadet rates it for grades up to 20 degrees and properties up to 2 acres, with a 22 HP, 725cc Kohler twin-cylinder engine turning a 46-inch fabricated AeroForce deck.
The frame is 2-by-2-inch tubular steel, and the steering column tilts to suit the rider. A 20-inch high-back seat on polymer suspension and a rubber floor mat take the edge off rough ground. An AGM battery handles starting. Warranty runs three years with no hour limit, plus limited lifetime coverage on the frame and deck.

excerpt: Fifty inches of fabricated AeroForce deck, a 25 HP Kohler V-twin and dual Hydro-Gear drives, with four-wheel Synchro-Steer control.
description:
Power comes from a 25 HP Kohler 7000 Series V-twin OHV engine, and the 50-inch AeroForce deck is fully fabricated rather than stamped. Dual Hydro-Gear EZT 2200 transaxles handle the zero-turn drive, and Synchro-Steer puts all four wheels under control, which steadies the machine on grades as steep as 20 degrees.
The seat is a 20-inch high back on polymer isolators and adjusts to the rider. Dual LED headlights cover early and late work. The frame is 2-by-2-inch tubular steel with automotive-grade corrosion resistance, riding on Turf Master 4-ply tires. Coverage runs three years with no hour limit, and the frame and deck shell carry a limited lifetime warranty.

excerpt: Kohler V-twin power, a fabricated 50-inch deck and Synchro-Steer four-wheel control for mowing grades without sliding.
description:
A fabricated 50-inch AeroForce deck sits under this zero turn, driven by a 25 HP Kohler 7000 Series V-twin OHV engine through a pair of Hydro-Gear EZT 2200 transaxles. Four-wheel Synchro-Steer control keeps the rear end planted on grades as steep as 20 degrees.
The frame is 2-by-2-inch tubular steel with automotive-grade corrosion resistance, carried on Turf Master 4-ply tires. The 20-inch high-back seat adjusts and rides on polymer isolators, and dual LED headlights extend the mowing window at either end of the day. Cub Cadet covers it for three years with no hour limit, with a limited lifetime warranty on the frame and deck shell.

excerpt: A 54-inch three-blade fabricated deck and 24 HP Kohler V-twin, with Hydro-Gear hydrostatic drive and dual LED headlights.
description:
Cutting comes from a 54-inch fabricated deck running three blades, turned by a 24 HP, 725cc Kohler 7000 Series V-twin OHV engine. A Hydro-Gear EZT hydrostatic transmission sets ground speed, topping out at 7 mph forward and 3.5 mph in reverse.
The frame is heavy square tubular steel. Front wheels measure 11 by 6 inches on 5-inch rims, rears 20 by 10 inches on 8-inch rims. Fuel capacity is 3.5 gallons, and dual LED headlights make early-morning and late-evening passes practical. A three-year consumer warranty applies.

excerpt: Kawasaki twin-cylinder power and a 60-inch fabricated AeroForce deck, sized for open ground running to four acres.
description:
Four acres is the working range here, handled by a 24 HP, 726cc Kawasaki FR730V twin-cylinder OHV engine and a heavy-duty 60-inch AeroForce fabricated deck. Dual hydrostatic transmissions drive the rear wheels, which is what makes the quick direction changes around beds and trees possible.
The frame is 2-by-2-inch tubular steel. Rider hardware runs to arm rests, a rubber floor mat, lap bars that adjust and carry shaped grips, and a 20-inch high back seat on polymer suspension, with leg room to spare. An AGM battery holds its charge through the off-season, and a bagging system is available separately. Warranty runs three years with no hour limit, plus limited lifetime coverage on frame and deck.

excerpt: Commercial-grade Kawasaki FX801 power under a reinforced 60-inch AeroForce Max deck, with ground speeds reaching 9 mph.
description:
This one sits at the heavy end of the Ultima range. An 852cc Kawasaki FX801 V-twin OHV engine, rated 25.5 HP, turns a 60-inch AeroForce Max deck built from 10-gauge reinforced steel, with low-maintenance spindles and three smooth-arc blades under a deep dome.
Dual hydrostatic rear-wheel transmissions are good for 9 mph forward and 3.5 mph in reverse, so wide open sections go by quickly. The frame is 1.5-by-3-inch tubular steel, stiff enough for the deck width while leaving routine service points reachable.

excerpt: A symmetric two-post lift rated at 10,000 pounds, with dual direct-drive cylinders, telescoping arms and locks every three inches.
description:
Built for full-size trucks, vans and passenger cars in a home shop or a working garage. Dual hydraulic direct-drive cylinders do the lifting, triple-telescoping drop-end arms reach awkward pickup points at a lower pad height, and safety locks engage every 3 inches in each column with a single-point release.
The columns stand on 17-by-19-inch A36 steel base plates and carry 53-inch carriages on self-lubricating UHMW polyethylene bearings. Half-inch aircraft-quality equalizer cables run over oversized sheaves to cut cable fatigue, and automatic arm restraints plus a padded overhead shutoff bar handle the rest. Maximum lift height is 79 inches and overall height is 145 inches, so ceiling clearance is worth measuring first. A four-piece 63 mm stackable adapter set and pads are included.

excerpt: An electric dump cart that carries up to 1,100 pounds and tips its bucket a full 90 degrees on hydraulic power.
description:
Hauling gravel, mulch or firewood by wheelbarrow gets old quickly. This cart takes up to 1,100 pounds and empties with a 48-volt hydraulic sealed piston that tips the bucket a full 90 degrees; the 8 cubic foot sealed bucket is a quick-change design.
Drive is self-propelled in both directions at up to 6 mph, with an articulated rear axle that lets the wheels follow uneven ground. Drive wheels measure 6 by 6.5-8 and rear wheels 11 by 4-4. Four 12-volt 20 Ah batteries total 1,000 watts, averaging about six hours of work per five-hour charge. A locking hand brake and upgraded brakes and throttle come standard, with a one-year chassis warranty.

excerpt: A steel plow blade measuring 82 by 19 inches that mounts to a two-inch front receiver and raises on a wireless remote.
description:
Made for SUVs and light-duty trucks fitted with a 2-inch Class III front receiver hitch. The blade measures 82 inches wide by 19 inches tall in powder-coated, rust-resistant steel, and a wireless remote raises and lowers it from behind the wheel rather than out in the weather.
Three angle positions lock in manually for pushing snow left, right or straight ahead. Integrated caster wheels make mounting and storage manageable, and the kit arrives complete with skid shoes, blade markers and a deflector, so nothing else has to be sourced. Assembly needs only common hand tools. Weight is 265 pounds, with a one-year manufacturer warranty.

excerpt: A tow-behind brush cutter with a 44-inch deck and electric-start Briggs engine, matched to an ATV, UTV or tractor.
description:
Land that has gone to seed needs more than a lawn mower. This tow-behind unit runs a 10.5 HP Briggs & Stratton OHV engine with electric start and cuts a 44-inch swath through heavy grass and through brush measuring as much as 3 inches across, covering roughly an acre in an hour.
The deck floats, riding over stumps and ruts instead of catching on them, and the blades pivot on impact rather than bending. It hitches behind an ATV, UTV or tractor, and what it takes down gets mulched on the spot.

excerpt: A high-capacity lawn vacuum with a 330-gallon collection system, built for properties that generate real leaf volume.
description:
Collection capacity is the number that matters most on a leaf vacuum, and this one holds 44 cubic feet, or 330 gallons, of leaves, clippings and yard debris. That translates to fewer trips to the pile over the course of a fall cleanup.
Suction comes from a 9.2 HP OHV engine, its cylinder sleeved in cast iron, and the hopper is set up to dump without a wrestling match. It suits medium to large properties where cleanup runs for hours rather than minutes.

excerpt: A 34-inch walk-behind brush mower with a 20 HP Briggs V-twin, three forward speeds and disc-brake power steering.
description:
The 34-inch brush deck reaches well outside the wheelbase, so the cut path runs right up against fence lines, trees and outbuildings without repositioning the machine. Discharge is to the side, and the deck pivots to follow ground contours.
Power comes from a 20 HP Briggs & Stratton Professional Series V-twin with electric start, 650cc of displacement, a pair of cylinder sleeves in cast iron, a spin-off oil filter and a full-pressure oil pump that keeps lubrication steady on side slopes. Three forward speeds and one reverse set the pace. Each wheel has its own disc brake on a hand lever, so squeezing one side pivots the mower around that wheel. Optional attachments fit.

excerpt: A self-propelled lawn and leaf vacuum with an onboard chipper, adjustable intake height and an all-steel impeller.
description:
A 9.2 HP, 301cc DR OHV engine drives both the suction and the self-propelled transmission, which offers three forward speeds and one reverse. EZ-Turn steering keeps it manageable around beds and narrow side yards, and intake height adjusts from 1 to 5 inches for bare turf or deep leaf cover.
The onboard chipper takes branches up to 2 inches, and material is compressed roughly ten to one into an 8 cubic foot bag rated for 80 pounds. Side zipper openings make emptying straightforward. The impeller is all steel and carries a lifetime warranty. The machine weighs 250 pounds on 14-by-4.5-inch front and 8-by-3-inch rear turf tread tires.

excerpt: A 15.5 HP walk-behind brush mower with electric start, disc-brake power steering and the reach to clear saplings 2.5 inches through.
description:
Thick brush, tall grass and small saplings are the working diet here. The 15.5 HP engine handles saplings measuring 2.5 inches across, and electric start means no rope pull before a long afternoon of clearing.
A full-pressure oil pump keeps the engine lubricated on inclines, which is what makes mowing slopes up to 20 degrees practical. Power steering comes from independent disc brakes on each wheel: hold one lever and the mower pivots around that side. Feathering the uphill brake helps it track straight across a slope rather than drifting downhill.

excerpt: A tri-fuel portable generator producing 13,000 surge and 10,500 running watts from gasoline, propane or natural gas.
description:
Fuel choice is the point of this one. It runs on gasoline, on propane, or on natural gas piped from a house line, which removes the storage problem when a long outage empties the local pumps. The cast-iron sleeved 460cc engine peaks at 13,000 watts of surge, 10,500 of it constant.
Starting is electric, with a recoil backup if the battery goes flat. Solid-fill tires cannot go flat, and the handles are set up for leverage over rough ground. The oversized muffler reduces noise, and its integral spark arrestor covers campgrounds and job sites where one is mandated. A carbon monoxide alert is built in. Setup out of the box amounts to fitting the wheels and handles and adding oil and fuel.

excerpt: Tri-fuel operation, 13,000 surge watts and a 50-amp plug for transfer-switch hookup, with push-button and remote start.
description:
Whole-house backup is the job this generator is sized for: 13,000 watts at surge and 10,500 constant from a 460cc engine, with a 50-amp plug that ties into a transfer switch. It burns gasoline, propane or natural gas, so refueling depends on whatever is available during an outage rather than one supply.
Starting happens at the push of a button or by remote, with recoil as a fallback. The power panel adds four 120-volt 20-amp GFCI outlets for tools and smaller loads. Solid-fill tires stay permanently inflated, high-leverage handles help over rough ground, and the oversized muffler carries a spark arrestor. A carbon monoxide alert is built in.

excerpt: A dual-fuel portable generator rated at 5,500 starting and 4,500 running watts, switching between gasoline and propane.
description:
A 224cc OHV engine supplies 5,500 starting watts and 4,500 running, enough for lights, a refrigerator, an air conditioner or a run of power tools. It burns gasoline or propane, so a stored tank covers the stretch when pumps are down.
MX2 technology draws full power from both the 120-volt and 240-volt receptacles, which suits RV use. The panel holds two 120-volt GFCI household outlets, a 120/240-volt 30-amp twist lock, a voltmeter and 12-volt DC charging posts. Low oil shutoff protects the engine, and the unit meets both EPA and CARB emissions requirements.

excerpt: A portable power station bundled with two 110-watt solar panels for recharging well away from a wall outlet.
description:
The bundle pairs the Delta 2 950 power station with two 110-watt solar panels, so the battery can be topped up from sunlight during a multi-day outage or a long stretch off grid. AC and DC input work as well when either is available.
Output runs through a pure sine wave inverter with low total harmonic distortion, which matters for laptops, phones and medical equipment that object to rough power. A digital display reports state of charge, output level and remaining runtime. The case is compact and built to travel.

excerpt: A high-capacity portable power station with pure sine wave output and a display that tracks charge and runtime.
description:
Sized for household backup and for trips well past the last outlet, the Delta 2 Max 1900 runs appliances, tools and electronics off a battery instead of an engine, with no fuel to store and no exhaust to vent.
Its inverter produces pure sine wave AC with low total harmonic distortion, which keeps laptops, phones and medical devices on clean power. Charging accepts solar, AC and DC input. The front display reports battery status, output and remaining runtime as it works, and the case is built to be carried and to take some knocking around.

excerpt: A 21-inch battery mower with the Select Cut multi-blade system and Touch Drive self-propel, running on a 56-volt pack.
description:
Cordless mowing, no gas can involved. The 21-inch deck runs the Select Cut multi-blade cutting system, and Touch Drive places self-propelled speed control at the handlebar, so pace changes happen without letting go of the grips.
The included 56-volt 10.0 Ah ARC Lithium battery runs up to 75 minutes on a charge, which covers most residential lots in a single session. The machine is built to hold up to regular work outdoors across seasons.

excerpt: A battery zero turn steered by wheel rather than lap bars, cutting up to 2.5 acres per charge on four included packs.
description:
e-STEER replaces lap bars with a steering wheel, so the machine handles like a car while still pivoting the way a zero turn does. Four independent brushless motors deliver output equivalent to a 22-horsepower gas engine across a 42-inch deck, without the noise or the fumes.
Peak Power technology pools up to six EGO 56-volt ARC Lithium batteries. The four 12.0 Ah packs included cover up to 2.5 acres per charge, and adding batteries extends that as far as the property requires. Ground speed runs 4 to 8 mph, the seat rides on adjustable hydraulic suspension, and an LCD switches between Control, Standard and Sport modes. Bluetooth, a USB charging port and LED lighting come as standard.

excerpt: Four brushless motors, ten cutting heights and 3-in-1 discharge on a 42-inch battery-powered zero turn deck.
description:
Peak output matches a 22-horsepower gas engine, split across four independent brushless motors, and e-STEER gives the machine a steering wheel in place of lap bars. An LCD offers Control, Standard and Sport modes, with ground speeds of 4 to 7 mph and 8 mph when traveling rather than cutting.
The 42-inch stamped steel deck carries two blades, ten cutting heights from 1.5 to 4.5 inches, and mulching, bagging and side-discharge use. Four 10.0 Ah batteries ship with it and cover up to 2 acres per charge, or 3 acres with six 10 Ah packs; an accessory box and the POWER+ Z6 charger are in the carton too. Construction is IPX4 weather resistant, with 32 LED headlights, Bluetooth for firmware updates and a hydraulic adjustable seat. Mower and batteries carry a five-year limited warranty.

excerpt: A 52-inch fabricated-deck battery zero turn with five brushless motors and six 12 Ah packs included, good for four acres.
description:
Five independent brushless motors put out the equivalent of 25 horsepower, and the 52-inch deck is fabricated from 10-gauge steel rather than stamped. Top speed is 8 mph, so open sections go by quickly.
Six 56-volt 12.0 Ah ARC Lithium batteries are included and cut up to 4 acres per charge, with room to add packs for more ground; the same battery platform runs other EGO tools. The charger fills all six in about four hours. Seat suspension adjusts, an LCD selects Control, Standard or Sport modes, and LED lighting, Bluetooth and a port for USB charging are fitted as standard. Mower, batteries and charger are covered for five years.

excerpt: A portable inverter that turns stored DC battery power into household AC current for vehicles, RVs and boats.
description:
An inverter converts DC from a battery into the AC current household electronics expect, which is what makes a laptop, a small appliance or a power tool usable away from a wall outlet. This one is built for automotive, RV and marine electrical systems.
The housing is compact and rugged enough for tight installs and regular transport, and the controls and indicators are simple to read while keeping an eye on output. Typical duty includes camping, off-road trips and time on the water, anywhere the power source is a battery rather than a breaker panel.

excerpt: A powder-coated steel trolley for the Enosign 65 plancha, with gas bottle storage, folding shelves and all-terrain wheels.
description:
Galvanized steel under a powder coat is what lets an outdoor cooking cart sit through rain and sun without rusting or fading. A compartment below holds the gas bottle out of sight, and a hanging bar along the frame keeps tongs and spatulas within reach.
Side shelves fold out for prep space and fold away when the cart is parked. All-terrain wheels move it across grass or gravel without a fight. It measures 90 by 50 by 85 centimeters and weighs 22 kilograms.

excerpt: A fully stainless steel cart for the Enosign 65 Inox plancha, with sliding side shelves and an enclosed gas bottle cabinet.
description:
Stainless throughout, this cart gives the Enosign 65 Inox gas plancha a proper home that still rolls. Four wheels carry it, two of them swiveling with brakes, so it stays put where it is set and moves when it needs to.
Two folding side shelves extend on a sliding system when more landing space is wanted for plates and trays. A door closes off the compartment where the gas bottle sits, and its long handle doubles as a rail for hanging accessories. Overall size is 126 by 57 by 76 centimeters, at 28 kilograms.

excerpt: A French-made gas plancha with twin cast burners, an enamelled double-wall cooking plate and a 150 to 360 degree range.
description:
Two circular cast burners sit under a double-walled cast plate finished in enamel certified for food contact. The double wall holds heat in the plate and spreads it, and the setting range runs from 150 to 360 degrees Celsius.
Ignition is electronic and works one-handed, with thermocouple safety at the burners. The plate joins the frame without a seam to trap grease, high edges contain spatter, and the surface resists scratching. The body is galvanized steel coated with charged polyester, and the burners are 7mm cast iron. Manufactured in France from repairable, recyclable materials, with a 10-year warranty on the burners. A soft-closing lid is available separately.
